T177: the platform must teach its own vocabulary. WorkHive puts domain acronyms straight onto the glass - MTBF beside a number, OEE on a card, SPI in a project summary. For a reliability engineer that is correct and efficient; for the audience this platform explicitly courts - new graduates, workers coming off paper - an unexplained acronym is a number they can neither act on nor argue with, and 'I did not understand the screen' is indistinguishable from 'the screen was wrong'. Fixed at FIRST USE in that line ('Earned value (EVM): schedule performance SPI ..., cost performance CPI ..., ... (budget at completion ₱..., earned value ₱...)'), because a glossary a reader has to go and find is a glossary they do not read. ★assistant.html IS EXCLUDED WITH ITS REASON: it carries a capability CATALOG describing every other page to the model ('...daily progress, EV/SPI/CPI, and sign-off'), which is model-facing rather than UI and double-counts vocabulary belonging to the pages it names - pages this gate scans on their own. T171: what an ISO-minded evaluator would check. Swept all 117 public pages for certification and compliance language, and the headline result is good AND worth stating precisely, because 'we claim no certifications' is easy to assert and had never been verified: there is NO WorkHive self-certification anywhere - no SOC 2, no ISO 27001, no 'GDPR-compliant', no HIPAA, no PCI-DSS, no bank-grade or military-grade security. All 30 raw hits were a standard the CUSTOMER is audited against (ISO 9001/14001/45001, DOLE OSHS), a PERSON's credential (TESDA NC II/III, CMRP, PSME/IIEE), or the skill matrix's own 'certified level' vocabulary. ★THE ONE REAL OVERCLAIM WAS A CATEGORY ERROR, NOT A BOAST: dole-iso-audit-trail-from-logbook said WorkHive logbook entries 'SATISFY Clause 10.2', the PM dashboard 'SATISFIES Clause 7.1.5', safety observations 'SATISFY Clause 9.1.1'. A clause is satisfied by an ORGANISATION's management system, evidenced by records - a tool holds the evidence, it cannot confer conformity - and the sentence reads as reassurance, so a plant could walk into a surveillance audit believing a feature had covered them. Rewritten to 'gives you the records Clause 10.2 asks you to retain' / 'evidences Clause 9.1.1', plus a callout stating the distinction outright: same value claimed, no false comfort. Live-verified rendering, 0 pageerrors. TWO ASSERTIONS: (clause) no feature may satisfy/meet/fulfil a NUMBERED clause - and note what is deliberately NOT caught, since 'the digital record satisfies three properties' and 'export patterns that satisfy auditors' both appear on that same page and are both fine, because a record CAN satisfy a property and an export CAN satisfy a sampling need; only a numbered clause as the object is the error; (selfcert) no page may claim a certification the platform lacks - zero today, guard-the-absence, because that is the single most tempting sentence to add to a sales page and the most expensive to be wrong about. Teeth proven on both.

T162: a promise to re-check is a promise. The competitor-comparison pages are the most perishable content on the platform and they are written WELL - every competitor price dated ('published entry pricing, August 2026'), sourced ('vendor published pricing and feature pages, accessed August 2026'), caveated ('SaaS pricing moves, confirm current terms with the vendor'), and generous to the competition ('the strongest mobile-first product in the category'). Nothing in the comparisons themselves needed fixing. ★THE RISK IS HIDDEN INSIDE THAT QUALITY: each page also prints 'Pricing verified against vendor and directory listings on 5 August 2026' and 'This comparison is reviewed quarterly for pricing and feature accuracy'. Those are not descriptions, they are COMMITMENTS with a clock running - and left alone they decay into the worst kind of claim, an explicit confident promise of currency printed beside prices nobody has re-checked in a year. A reader trusts the page MORE because of that sentence, which is precisely what makes it expensive when it stops being true. THE ASSERTION: where a page states a verification date AND a review cadence, the date must still be inside the cadence it promised (quarterly = 92 days). Measured 2026-08-26: 3 pages, all verified 5 August 2026, 21 days old and comfortably inside. ★THIS GATE IS BUILT TO GO RED - around 5 November 2026 for these three, unless someone re-verifies. That is the point, not a defect: it converts a marketing sentence into a maintained obligation, and the fix when it fires is a real one (re-check the prices and move the date, or delete the commitment). NO GRACE PERIOD, deliberately - the page names its own cadence, so the cadence is the bar; the passing output prints the days remaining so it arrives as a countdown rather than a surprise. Teeth proven by ageing one date to 5 January: 233d against a 92d promise, exit 1.

T161: content ages with supervision, not heroics. A statistic on a public page is a claim a reader - or an answer engine - will repeat, and the dangerous shape is not an OLD year but a year that silently became a LIE: 'as of 2024, the average plant...' was true when written and is quietly false now, because nobody re-reads a sentence that already shipped. ★THE INVENTORY CHANGED WHAT THIS GATE ASSERTS, and that is the lesson: a first pass across 114 public pages flagged 33 'claims 3+ years old' and nearly every one was a CITATION or a STANDARD EDITION - ISO 14224 (2016), CIBSE Guide D:2015, IEC 62305:2010, DENR DAO 2016-08, Nakajima 1988 for the origin of OEE. Those years are part of the source's IDENTITY; flagging them would have demanded the pages stop citing their standards precisely, the exact opposite of the goal, and 33 false findings on the way. SO IT ASSERTS THE SHAPE, NOT THE AGE. Two things rot and neither is a citation: (as-of) a present-tense claim pinned to a past year - 'as of 2024', 'currently ... 2023', 'latest figures 2022' - allowed only within the current year and the two before it, the window SLIDING with the clock so the gate keeps supervising without anyone re-tuning it; and (future) a statistic dated in a year that has not happened, always a typo or a template copy, which reads as authoritative until someone checks. BOTH ARE ZERO TODAY across 115 pages - this is a guard-the-absence gate in the no-clock-driven-push family, because a property that holds by CARE rather than by structure lapses in silence. Teeth proven on both shapes at once: an injected 'as of 2021' and a '2029 survey' -> 2 flagged, exit 1.

T154: machine-readable truth = human-readable truth. JSON-LD is what an answer engine QUOTES when it cites this platform, and nobody proofreads it because nobody SEES it - so it drifts away from the page underneath and keeps being served, confidently, to the machines that summarize us. TWO CONTRACTS, both born from real drift. FAQ: every FAQPage Question name must appear in the page's visible text - the class T1 caught on the landing page, where the LD still told the provisioning-waitlist story after the page had moved to instant signup; an FAQ rich result PROMISES the page answers that question, so if the words are not there the promise is to content that does not exist (508 questions across 115 public pages, all present). NAME: an Article headline must still be recognisable as the page's own og:title/<title> - FOUND HERE, predictive-alert-thresholds-plants had been retitled to lead with 'ISO 10816 Vibration Thresholds and Predictive Alert Limits', a deliberate move toward the citable standard, while its LD headline kept the older vaguer 'Predictive Alert Thresholds for Industrial Plants', so an answer engine reading the structured data got the version WITHOUT the ISO anchor that makes the page worth citing (synced; 53 headlines now match). ★HowToStep NAMES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GATED, AND THE EXCLUSION IS THE FINDING: a first pass flagged 31 'gaps' across 12 HowTo pages and every one was editorial paraphrase - the OEE guide's LD says 'Measure planned production time' where the page heads that section 'Step 1: Planned Production Time'. Same step, different register. A step name is a LABEL for a procedure; demanding substring identity would have shipped 31 false findings and taught everyone to ignore this gate. The FAQ question and the headline are different in kind - both are read VERBATIM by their consumers, so identity is the actual contract there. Teeth proven on BOTH halves: a fabricated question and a reverted headline, 2 flagged, exit 1.

T158: a canonical must name a URL that EXISTS. rel=canonical is a claim - 'the real version of this page lives here' - and when the URL it names does not exist, the page tells every crawler its authoritative copy is at nothing. FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-26, VERIFIED AGAINST PRODUCTION rather than inferred: workhiveph.com/workhive/public-feed.html returned 404 while workhiveph.com/public-feed.html returned 200, and FIFTEEN pages shipped the dead form - a /workhive/ segment left over from an earlier deploy path, still being served long after the site moved to the domain root. ★WHY IT SURVIVED EVERY EXISTING CHECK: they all asked whether a canonical was PRESENT, and all 15 were present, well-formed, absolute and unique - and pointed at a 404. Presence is the easy half of a claim; this gate checks the half that costs something. ★THE ONE THAT MATTERED MOST was public-feed, the anonymous shop window and the only one of the 15 meant to be found by strangers: a shared link to it carried a signal saying the real page was elsewhere, at a URL that does not resolve. Now 145 on-site canonicals all name a page that exists. STATIC BY DESIGN - the path IS the defect, and a live HTTP check would make the gate depend on the network to state a fact about a string. TEETH PROVEN by re-breaking public-feed's canonical: 1 flagged, exit 1.

T160: the SEO funnel must not jump while you read it. CLS is where a page loses a searcher without erroring - text settles, the reader's eye is already moving, and the line they were on is somewhere else - and on the funnel it costs twice, because Core Web Vitals feed ranking, so the pages most dependent on search were the ones shifting. MEASURED, ISOLATED, THEN FIXED. The learn template shifted 0.384 CLS at 390, nearly 4x the 0.1 bar. ★THE RECORDED SUSPICION WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO: the note blamed an element injected at ~1s, and a MutationObserver armed alongside the shift observer recorded NO insertion of any size. The timeline showed a 0.182 shift at 903ms and document.fonts.ready at 907ms; blocking the font stylesheet took CLS to 0.000 while blocking the Tailwind CDN only reached 0.156. The font swap was the whole cause. THE FIX was one parameter - display=swap to display=optional across 113 public pages: optional gives the font ~100ms then never swaps, so the page cannot jump, and measured on a real load it STILL renders Poppins. The only reader who now sees the fallback is on a genuinely slow first load, which is exactly the reader who previously got the jump instead. Verified 0.000 CLS across learn, tools and the landing page. ★IT ASSERTS THE PARAMETER, NOT A CLS NUMBER: a lab CLS reading on loopback is optimistic and noisy, and a gate that fails intermittently gets ignored - the parameter is deterministic and it IS the defect.

T3/T153: the calculator pages state the account requirement. The 60 /tools/ pages are the top of the funnel - a searcher looking for 'OEE calculator' lands on one, and what it promises decides whether the next click is trust or a bounce. MEASURED 2026-08-26 and the human-facing story is HONEST: none of the 60 embeds a calculator (they are landing pages that explain a calculation and hand off) and every one says so plainly - 'free with a WorkHive account. Sign-up takes about 30 seconds.' ZERO still carry the 'no sign-up needed' claim T3 recorded, which linked into a gated page and was false twice over. The gate keeps a fixed claim fixed, because that wording lived in a TEMPLATE - it came back everywhere at once when it came back at all. ★A RECORDED FINDING IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ENFORCE: every one of the 60 declares JSON-LD @type SoftwareApplication with an Offer of price 0 and a url pointing at the LANDING page, so a search or answer engine reads 'there is a free web application here', follows the url, and finds a page about an application that lives somewhere else. The human CTA is honest; the MACHINE claim overclaims. Pointing that url at the app would make it true in one line, but rewriting the structured data of 60 pages changes how the platform is presented in search - an outward-facing decision nobody can quietly reverse - so it is written up for Ian rather than done. Teeth-proven by restoring the exact old wording.

T156: a shared link should look intentional. T125 established what sharing here actually looks like - workers paste links into Viber and Messenger group chats - which makes the Open Graph card the first thing most people see of a page, often before the page itself. THE FINDING: 60 of ~116 public pages shipped NO og:image and no twitter:card, and they were all the /tools/ CALCULATORS - the top of the funnel, the pages most likely to be shared by a worker who just used one. Every one rendered as a bare grey link while the learn cluster's 53 articles rendered a proper card. public-feed had an image and a title but no og:description, so its card showed a headline, a picture, and whatever text the platform chose to guess. Fixed by reusing the SAME asset the learn cluster already uses rather than inventing a second one: two social images drift and one ends up stale. ★IT CHECKS THE IMAGE FILE EXISTS, not merely that the tag does - a card pointing at a missing PNG renders exactly like a card with no image, and the tag being present makes it look handled, which is the worst combination because nobody re-checks a field that is filled in. App pages are deliberately out of scope: a signed-in surface behind an auth wall is not shared to a group chat. Teeth-proven both ways - card removed RED, image pointed at a missing file RED.

T152: the teaching cluster is navigable in BOTH directions. 53 articles only teach as a cluster if a reader can move through them, and two different failures break that while being invisible to each other. AN ORPHAN is an article no hub link reaches: it exists, it is indexed, a searcher can land on it, and nobody browsing the library will ever find it - writing it was work that reaches nobody. A DEAD END is an article that links onward to nothing: a reader who finishes it has to go back and start again, which is where a session ends. Measured: 53 articles, 53 reachable from the hub, ZERO orphans, ZERO dead ends, and the hub links to nothing missing. The gate keeps it that way, because adding an article and forgetting the hub entry is a one-line omission nobody notices. ★IT ALSO CHECKS THE REVERSE OF AN ORPHAN - a hub link to an article that does not exist - because a library index offering a guide that 404s is worse than not listing it, and this cluster has been renamed before. ★AND ONWARD LINKS MUST REACH OTHER LEARN ARTICLES, not merely somewhere: a page whose only outbound link is a signup CTA is a dead end for a reader who came to learn, however many links it technically has. Teeth-proven by renaming one hub slug, which fired BOTH arms at once - the article became an orphan and the hub gained a promise it could not keep.

T151: a searcher's question answered above the fold, swept across all 53 learn articles. Somebody arrives from a search result with a question the snippet promised this page answers; what they meet in the first screen decides whether they stay, and the failure mode is not a broken page but one that opens with throat-clearing and buries the answer four scrolls down. ★THE ORACLE IS ANSWER-PRESENCE, NOT META-VERBATIM - T151 learned that the hard way when an earlier pass checked whether the meta description's words appeared on the page and produced a false red, because a description SUMMARIZES rather than quotes. Four assertions per article: an H1 exists; substantive opening prose follows it; that opening carries a distinctive term from the title; and a freshness stamp is visible, because a searcher landing on undated maintenance guidance cannot tell if it is current. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANY VERDICT WAS TRUSTED, each found by READING the flags rather than acting on them: a {3,} filter silently dropped this platform's most important short terms (PM, AI, OEE) so an article opening 'Most Philippine plants run PMs' read as off-topic; an exact match called 'measurement' a miss for a title saying 'Measuring'; and scanning only

elements flagged the WorkHive-vs-MaintainX page, which opens with a textbook answer ('Choose MaintainX if... Choose WorkHive if...') written in a

of lines - the

tags it found were the byline and a repeated pricing disclaimer, so the gate read the furniture and missed the answer. It now reads VISIBLE TEXT, and allows one paragraph of runway, because enforcing sentence-one would legislate prose style rather than measure arrival. All 53 pass. Mutation-proven both ways: burying an answer behind preamble goes RED, and stripping a freshness stamp goes RED.

T133: absent is not zero, especially in pesos. whFmtPeso exists for one recorded reason - Number(null) is 0 and finite, so a null amount slips through as a confident 0.00. A filed top-up of PHP300 once rendered as PHP0.00 and a ledger line of unknown value rendered as +0, a sentence saying the entry moved nothing. The helper prints a GAP for absent and still prints 0 for a real zero, because a person can act on 'we do not know' and cannot act on a wrong number. THE FINDINGS: founder-console - the owner's own cockpit - had ZERO adoption and a formatter that was literally Number(n || 0), the bug itself, while the same file carried a note saying a money number frozen at zero 'does not read as by design, it reads as a feed that died'; its GCash top-up row had no null guard at all. marketplace-seller's earnings formatter used Number(n), so an absent figure printed NaN on the dashboard of the person being paid. marketplace's service picker guarded <= 0, which catches null but NOT undefined - Number(undefined) is NaN and NaN <= 0 is FALSE - so an absent rate fell through as NaN to a buyer. All routed through the helper. ★THE GATE'S OWN FIRST RUN FLAGGED FOUR FALSE POSITIVES and they were NOT acted on: a ternary spans lines, so the GUARDED FALLBACK half of `whFmtPeso(n) : '+Number(n||0)` looked hand-rolled because the helper sat on the line above. 'Fixing' those would have damaged correct code whose fallback exists so the page still renders when utils.js has not loaded. It now reads a window and honours an explicit null branch. Scoped to money surfaces by design - a gate policing every peso sign would catch option labels and prose and be switched off.

T166: 'who sees this?' answered where it is WRITTEN. Every write surface makes a person decide how candid to be, and that decision happens at the composer - answering it on a welcome card, a help page or a toast after the fact is answering it too late or to the wrong person. THE FINDING: voice-journal.html had ZERO audience statements while being the platform's MOST private surface - voice_journal_entries carries auth.uid() = auth_uid on read, update AND delete, so nobody else in the hive can reach a single row. The only place a worker was ever told lived on hive.html's join-flow welcome card: seen once, on a different page, at a moment they were not writing anything personal. A privacy guarantee a person cannot see is one they cannot rely on. THE WORDING IS READ OFF THE RLS, NEVER FROM MEMORY, and this trajectory carries the scar - a welcome card written the same week claimed the Voice Journal was the ONLY worker-private surface while the policies said otherwise (skill_profiles, badges and exam_attempts are auth_uid-scoped too). So the gate checks BOTH ENDS: the claim on the page AND the policies in the database, failing if a page claims a privacy the policies do not give - a promise the database does not keep being worse than no promise at all. Deliberately a SHORT NAMED LIST of surfaces where a person commits words others might read, not every input on the platform: a gate demanding an audience label on search boxes and filters would be switched off within a week. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix voice-journal.

Seller dashboard + hidden pages are reachable (the All Tools grid shows a seller their own dashboard, and global search finds curated-out pages like the audit trail by name — driven live in a browser, not asserted from the registry)

Celebration proportionality (the tier ladder and the round-number ladder live in different files and must not fire full-screen modals on consecutive level-ups — two celebrations in a row is one interruption, and it devalues the larger)

T18: a read-gate must not depend on an event that may never fire. skillmatrix gates its exam behind 'read the lesson first' - the Take-exam button starts disabled and a scroll handler enables it once the reader reaches the bottom. Correct intent, and it had a hole: the button was enabled ONLY from inside that handler. ★A LESSON WHOSE CONTENT FITS THE BOX NEVER SCROLLS, so the scroll event never fires, checkScroll never runs, and the reader is left in front of a permanently disabled 'Take exam' beside a hint telling them to scroll something that does not scroll - with no way out of that screen but closing it. Latent only because every lesson written so far happens to overflow, and lesson bodies are AUTHORED CONTENT, so the first short one ships the trap to whoever writes it. FIXED by evaluating the gate once at open, after the scroll reset: self-correcting, because for a non-scrolling box scrollTop + clientHeight already exceeds scrollHeight - 80 so the check passes immediately, while a long lesson at scrollTop 0 still fails it and the gate holds. ★VERIFIED LIVE ON BOTH BRANCHES, since the risk of this fix is that it opens the gate for everyone: long content (scrollHeight 822 vs clientHeight 502) still reports disabled=true with the hint shown, short content (54 vs 54) reports disabled=false with the hint cleared, 0 pageerrors. ★AND THE GATE ITSELF FAILED ITS FIRST TEETH TEST: the invocation count matched `function checkScroll()` - the DECLARATION - so deleting the real call still left a count of 1 and it reported PASS on the exact defect it exists for. A negative lookbehind for 'function ' fixed it; the teeth test refusing to go red is the only reason that was caught. Narrow by design: this is one known control, and inferring 'enabled only by an event' across the platform would be guessing at intent.

T159: the page must say which language it is in. A screen reader picks its pronunciation rules from <html lang>, so Filipino text announced under lang='en' comes out as English phonemes applied to Tagalog - not accented, but unrecoverable. WCAG 3.1.1 asks for the page's language and 3.1.2 that a change of language be marked. ★THE HARD HALF IS THAT THIS PLATFORM IS BILINGUAL BY TOGGLE, NOT BY URL: one page, _t(en, fil) at every string, and a wh_lang preference - so the declaration is not a static fact set at build time, it has to FOLLOW the toggle, which is exactly the half a static audit misses. MEASURED and the discipline is clean: all 156 public pages declare <html lang> (none silent); utils.js:219 sets documentElement.lang from the stored locale on EVERY page load, so a reader who chose Filipino gets the right declaration even on pages with no translation engine of their own; and all three pages that WRITE wh_lang (index, analytics, analytics-report) also assign documentElement.lang in their toggle handler, so switching mid-session updates the declaration without a reload. TWO ASSERTIONS: every public page carries <html lang>, and any page that writes the wh_lang preference must also assign documentElement.lang - a toggle that changes the words while leaving the declaration behind is WORSE than no toggle, because the page then asserts a language it is not in. ★NO hreflang IS ASSERTED, deliberately rather than by omission: hreflang describes ALTERNATE URLs for the same content and this platform has none - the locale lives in localStorage, so /learn/x is one URL serving whichever language the reader chose, and demanding hreflang would be demanding a second site. Whether to publish a Filipino public corpus at all is T159's open posture question and Ian's to answer; this gate holds the part that is true under either answer. Teeth proven on both halves.

T106's arrival-fidelity oracle for EMAIL. Every 'View in WorkHive' link in send-report-email pointed at a bare page root, so a PM Overdue report - a document whose entire subject IS the overdue set - landed its reader on the unfiltered schedule, and both logbook reports landed on that page's default MINE view while the report itself is hive-wide: T19's two-windows-one-metric mismatch arriving by email, at whoever the supervisor forwarded it to. Measured before changing anything - ?filter=overdue is a real chip value on pm-scheduler AND genuinely filters (live: ontrack 0 rows, duesoon 2, overdue 10 vs 10 bare), so the parameter works rather than merely highlighting a chip. THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERS is not that links carry params but that every param they carry is one the TARGET PAGE ACTUALLY READS, checked against the generated param_route_registry: a link decorated with ?window=7d would look more specific while delivering nothing, which is worse than a bare link because it reads as context that was never handed over. Also asserts every target page exists - a link into a renamed page is a dead end reached from an inbox, where nobody can press Retry. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: that all eight carry a param; five target analytics.html and project-manager.html, which read NO params at all, so their links are already as specific as those pages allow and demanding more would push someone to invent one that does nothing. Resurrection BOTH ways: RED on the pre-fix bare links, and RED again on a mutation adding a plausible ?window=90d that analytics never reads.

T107's one-honest-concept oracle for 'things for me'. The hive board's bell held four entries on the live board - PM Due Soon, Assets With PM Overdue, Open work orders, Low stock - every one a PLANT CONDITION already painted as a tile on the same page and again in alert-hub, blended with the approval entries, which are the only ones actually about the person reading them: one bell, two concepts, no way to tell which you were looking at. And the only unread signal was a 3% white tint on a dark surface, present in code and invisible in use, so a badge over ten rows gave no way to see WHICH were new. Asserts STRUCTURE, never wording: the two lanes are named, the plant lane links to the surface that owns those conditions, unread carries a marker BOTH a sighted user and a screen reader can find, and every pushNotif type is classified - a new one lands here as a decision rather than drifting into whichever lane the default sends it. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix page for 3 of 4, and the 4th mutation-proven with an injected 'mention' producer.

T23: the window on the CHIP must be the window in the EMAIL (2026-08-27). The four selectable reports cover wildly different periods — Shift Handover is the last EIGHT HOURS, Failure Digest the last 7 days, Predictive the last NINETY DAYS, PM Overdue a current-status snapshot — and the chooser showed a coloured dot and a label. A supervisor could send an 8-hour snapshot and a quarter of history to their boss in one email with nothing on screen distinguishing them, which is T23's own open question ('what is actually IN each of the 4 chips') answered as a defect. ★THE WINDOW WAS NEVER UNKNOWN: send-report-email's REPORT_META has carried it all along and prints it INSIDE the delivered email — it simply never reached the person CHOOSING. Now on every selectable chip, verified live: 'PM Overdue · current status as of this report', 'Shift Handover · last 8 hours', 'Predictive · last 90 days'. ★AND THAT PUTS A SECOND COPY OF A SERVER FACT IN THE CLIENT, the hazard this repo already names (two windows, one metric name) — two copies that can drift are worse than one copy nobody can see, unless something asserts they agree. This gate is that assertion: every offered id must exist in REPORT_META and every stated window must match the server string exactly; a phase3 chip may omit its window because it cannot be sent, so it promises nothing. ★ITS OWN SELF-TEST CAUGHT ITS OWN BUG: the first parser put an OPTIONAL window group behind a lazy prefix, and a lazy quantifier always prefers to skip the optional group — five logic cases passed while the live check reported four chips 'stating no window' that plainly stated one. Matching the row first and reading inside it fixed it. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases) incl. a drifted window, a selectable chip with none, and an id the server does not know. Static, read-only.

T29: acting on an alert must make the ALERT GO AWAY (2026-08-27). An alert inbox that never empties is an inbox people stop reading, so the chain has to close: the alert names an action, links to where that action is taken, and DOING it removes the alert — with nobody marking anything by hand. ★THE CLOSURE IS STRUCTURAL, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST KIND: alert-hub's PM alerts are DERIVED, not stored — they come from v_pm_scope_items_truth filtered is_overdue=true, so there is no status to update and no second write to forget. Complete the PM and the row simply stops matching. PROVEN LIVE rather than reasoned: inserting a 'done' completion for an overdue scope item inside a transaction takes its overdue count 1 → 0 and moves days_until_due −34 → +7, then rolls back with zero residue. ★TWO ASSERTIONS, because either alone is a half-truth — THE LINK EXISTS (an href to pm-scheduler for the NAMED asset plus an action label; an alert that states a problem and offers no way to it is a notification, not an inbox item) and THE CONDITION CLEARS (a link to a surface that does not actually resolve the alert leaves the loop open while looking closed). ★The gate's own link check was wrong first: a lazy any-character match ending at the first closing brace stopped INSIDE the first nested brace — inside a template expression, well before href and actionLabel — and reported a correctly-linked alert as offering no way to act. Read as a plain forward window now, because that is what the block is.

T94: a wallet must not offer credits that are already spoken for (2026-08-27). Listing HOLDS credits — guard_listing_requires_reservation writes a credit_reservations row, sweep_listing_holding_fee eats into it monthly, release_reservation_on_delist gives it back — and the seller page SAYS so at listing time ('holds ₱50 in credits'). Held credits are not spendable. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY COMPUTED THE SPLIT: seller_credit_balance(worker_name) returns available / reserved / total, where available is the ledger balance MINUS everything held. The wallet card called provider_credit_balance() instead — the ledger sum alone — and labelled it the balance, so a seller with live listings saw a number larger than they could spend, on the same page that had just told them listing would hold some of it. Not a missing feature: the glass was reading the wrong one of three numbers that were already sitting there, the 'built but never called' shape with money in it. ★THE HEADLINE FIGURE IS DELIBERATELY NOT SWAPPED: provider_credit_balance distinguishes a person-owned provider (shows the PERSON's balance) from a hive-owned one (shows the HIVE's), and its own comment records why — 'two cards for one human showing different numbers is how this defect stayed invisible'. seller_credit_balance is person-keyed, so replacing the call wholesale would silently change WHICH ACCOUNT a hive-owned card reports: fixing one money defect by introducing another. The total stays; the HELD figure is added beside it, and renders only when something is actually held (a 'reserved ₱0' on every wallet teaches people to stop reading the card). ★MEASURED LIVE: credit_reservations is empty on this stack, so the gate CREATES a 50-credit hold inside a transaction and rolls it back — available=-50, reserved=50, total=0, split exact, 0 rows left. The probe row references a real listing because the table enforces num_nonnulls(listing_id, request_id)=1. Teeth (--selftest): a single-balance wallet goes RED, fetching the split but not showing it still goes RED, fetching AND naming it passes.

T11: a deduction that moved NOTHING must not read as success (2026-08-27). Two workers finish repairs on the same part; inventory_deduct locks the item FOR UPDATE so the race is serialised, and the loser's call runs against an empty shelf. ★WHAT THE LOSER GOT, MEASURED LIVE (real item set to 0 inside a rolled-back transaction): `v_qty := GREATEST(0, v_qty - p_qty)` CLAMPS instead of refusing, so asking for 1 with 0 on the shelf returned 0, wrote a ledger row with qty_change 0, changed nothing, and raised NO error. Every caller checked only `error`, so the worker was told 'Entry saved' while their entry claimed a part the shelf never gave up — the shelf and the system disagreeing silently, which is the one thing this trajectory exists to prevent. ★AND THE RETURN VALUE CANNOT TELL THEM APART: it is the new quantity, and 'took the last one' and 'there were none' both end at 0. The LEDGER row can, because it records what MOVED — so callers pass p_txn_id (the function always accepted one) and read that row back through whDeductMoved(); verified under RLS that a member can read their own hive's inventory_transactions row. ★THREE SITES, NOT ONE: logbook's SAVE path, logbook's EDIT path, and inventory's Use modal — and inventory additionally cached `addTransaction(..., -qty, ...)`, recording the amount ASKED, so the page's own transaction list claimed a movement the database never made; it now records what moved. The first version of this GATE had the same disease it was built to catch, grading only the first call it found with re.search while two others kept the defect. ★TEETH (--selftest): the pre-fix error-only shape goes RED, an id passed but never read back goes RED, id+readback+comparison passes, and every live site is asserted green. The DB half rolls back and re-reads the shelf to prove it.

T19: hiding a plant alert is a HIVE action and must say so (2026-08-27). alert_dismissals is keyed onConflict 'hive_id,alert_key' — ONE row per alert per hive — so every control that writes it changes what the WHOLE CREW sees: marking handled, snoozing, and marking seen alike. Nothing about the surface said that. The local state is `_seen`, the control is an aria-pressed toggle, the copy was two words: everything reads personal bookmark while the write is shared state. ★THE FAILURE IS WRITTEN IN dismissAlert's OWN COMMENT — 'a plant alert quietly blinded for the whole crew by someone who thought they were tidying their own view' — and that path was fixed when it was written while its SIBLING acknowledgeAlert was not: nothing about scope on the way in, and on the way out (un-marking DELETES the hive's row and returns the alert to unseen for everyone) nothing at all, so the crew could watch an alert reappear with no idea who or why. Both now name the scope and the actor, in EN and FIL. ★THE RULE: every user-facing message on a successful alert_dismissals write must name the scope, matched by MEANING across both languages rather than a fixed sentence — the copy ships bilingual via _t(en, fil), and a gate that pins wording punishes improving it. ★TEETH ARE THE PRE-FIX WORLD VERBATIM (--selftest, 5 cases): the old `_t('Marked seen', 'Minarkahang nakita')` is the 'two words with no scope' RED, and the old un-mark is the 'silent write' RED; a read-only query owes nothing and stays green. ★The gate's own window was wrong first and its selftest caught it: a fixed 900-char scan ended before both announcements (they sit past a writeAuditLog call and a long comment) and reported two correct paths as silent, so the search is now bounded by the `catch (` that actually ends the success path.

T7: the code still works, and the door is still shut (2026-08-27). A removed worker usually still HAS the invite code — read aloud at a briefing, sitting in a chat thread — so rejoining is not an edge case, it is the next thing that happens, and it has two halves that must agree. ★THE DOOR, asserted LIVE: join_hive_by_code refuses a kicked member twice over — by auth identity, and again by (hive, worker_name) so a second account cannot walk a ban back in. Both are driven, because 'the function has an IF' is not 'the function refuses', and the second branch only fires for an identity with no membership row at all, which is exactly the shape a reading of the source talks itself out of. ★AND THE SENTENCE: a refusal reaching a person as a raw code, or as 'could not join', says the app is broken rather than that a decision was made about them. hive.html must key on HIVE_MEMBER_KICKED and say WHAT (removed) and WHAT NOW (a way that is not retrying the code, since retrying is the one action that cannot work) — matched by MEANING, not a fixed sentence, because a fixed sentence is a gate that fails when someone improves the wording. Distinct from removal-tells-the-worker (T25), which covers the removed worker's ARRIVAL; this covers the door they knock on afterwards. ★SAFETY: the kicked state is created inside a transaction and ROLLED BACK, verified by re-reading the member's status. ★TEETH (--teeth): Postgres has transactional DDL, so the run replaces join_hive_by_code with a permissive version INSIDE the same transaction — both branches then report 'allowed' and the gate fails naming both, while the definition is re-read afterwards to prove the real function came back. A green teeth run would mean this gate cannot see an open door. ★The copy check itself was caught wrong by its own selftest first: a naive quote-to-quote regex paired the closing quote of one literal with the opening quote of the next and read the CODE between them, so a correct page looked silent.

PERSONA TASK-SUCCESS - can a DIVERSE human finish the money task, not just an idealised one? (Ian 2026-07-31: consider the diversity of human beings.) Every journey in the bank implicitly walked a competent, sighted, literate, English-reading, fast-network, calm user, and almost none of this platform's real users are all six at once - PH plant technicians in their fifties, first-time e-wallet users, someone outdoors in glare wearing gloves, someone on 3G. DIVERSITY IS NOT A PAGE PROPERTY, it is WHO IS WALKING, so it lives on the journey axis. DIVISION OF LABOUR, deliberately: UFAI grades the PAGE (validate_service_ufai_deep measures 390/1280 tap targets and overflow), validate_i18n_coverage owns language, validate_clickable_keyboard_a11y owns keyboard - none can answer 'could THIS PERSON complete THIS TASK'. The 25 personas and their journey pairings live in tools/service_personas.mjs as RUNTIME CONDITIONS (viewport, zoom, colour filter, throttle, locale, input delay), not comments, and 129 unpaired combinations are recorded WITH REASONS rather than dropped - 25 personas x 7 families is 175 walks nobody runs, and an unrunnable matrix silently becomes an unrun one. Seven checks on the families where failure costs pesos: 12 states carry DISTINCT TEXT labels not colour alone (P-COLORBLIND); the release screen discloses who gets what, that the platform never holds the money, and what happens if the job was bad (P-SCAMWARY, the persona who decides whether this economy works at all); the min-balance refusal is announced AND says how to fix it (P-UNBANKED); the release resists a double tap (P-IMPULSIVE); money terms are translatable (P-FILIPINO); the map has a text equivalent, since a map is unusable by a screen reader and without a list discovery is closed entirely (P-SCREENREADER); and a 48px target floor (P-GLOVED, a real industrial constraint). ITS OWN FIRST TWO READINGS WERE INSTRUMENT BUGS: it reported the 12 status labels MISSING because its regex assumed quoted object keys while the source uses bare ones, and reported the min-balance refusal owed because it read only marketplace.html while the message lives on marketplace-seller.html. Both are fixed and both are why it now reads the real SVC_CHIP mapping across BOTH money surfaces instead of pattern-matching one.

CREDIT SOLVENCY - are the credits given away backed by anything? MARKETPLACE_CREDIT_SUSTAINABILITY §5 named liability cover the number that matters, and §4.5 named spending the float the most dangerous failure mode BECAUSE IT IS INVISIBLE UNTIL IT IS FATAL. Credits enter three ways and they are NOT equal: topup is backed by CASH (a provider paid GCash), cashback is backed by REVENUE (funded out of commission, and the hive_service_settings CHECK already refuses cashback_pct > commission_pct + listing_fee_pct so it cannot outrun the take per transaction), and voucher_grant is backed by NOTHING - platform-funded acquisition minted from thin air. Vouchers are therefore the LIVE GAP: nothing currently bounds them, and a generous promo is indistinguishable from an accident until the float is gone. The invariant held here is `unbacked credits (vouchers) <= credits actually EARNED (commission)` - if the platform has given away more than it has ever earned, it is funding acquisition out of other people's prepayments, which works right up until they spend them. ALSO ASSERTED: a negative CONSUMER balance is impossible by construction (consumers only receive cashback and spend it), so one appearing means credits were spent that were never minted; a negative PROVIDER balance is expected and fine, since commission is debited on completion and min_list_balance is what keeps wallets funded. The arithmetic is a pure function so the self-test proves it catches over-granting and negative consumer balances and passes a healthy ledger WITHOUT needing the real ledger in any particular state - and an empty ledger PASSES vacuously while saying so, rather than reporting a false green. Reads service_credit_ledger via docker exec psql; skips when the DB is down.

PAYMENT RAILS - three GCash accounts meet in this product and only ONE of them may ever be on a given screen. WorkHive has no business registration and therefore no merchant account, so every rail is a PERSONAL number: a buyer pays the PROVIDER's own GCash directly and the platform never touches it; a provider tops up credits by paying the FOUNDER's personal 0995 009 2416; a credits spend moves no GCash at all, being a ledger transfer between two wallets. THE INVARIANT: the founder's number may appear ONLY on the provider's top-up card. Put it on a buyer-facing payment step and the buyer sends job money to a person who is not party to the job, cannot fulfil it, and cannot reconcile it against any request - and NOTHING ERRORS. The money is not lost to a bug but to a stranger's honest reading of the screen, which is worse, because nobody finds out until the provider asks where their payment is. This is also the exact friction Ian named by hand ('I want it hassle free for my users, like the hassle of payment two gcash accounts'): a buyer must see exactly one number, the provider's. Four assertions: every occurrence of the founder number sits on an allowed surface; no buyer-facing payment surface contains it in ANY spacing or punctuation (the regex tolerates '0995 009 2416', '0995-009-2416' and '09950092416' as one number); the buyer's confirm step states that WorkHive holds no money, which is the sentence a wary first-timer actually decides on; and that step names the PROVIDER as payee so 'who do I pay' has one answer where it is asked. Comments and doc blocks are stripped before matching - only RENDERED strings can mislead a person. Teeth: planting the founder's number on marketplace.html's payment step makes this FAIL naming that surface and that consequence; selftest proves all four failures are caught and a correct topology passes. Static, fast, no DB.

HIVE-CAPTURE INVARIANT — a load-time hive capture is only safe while nothing can change the active hive mid-page. marketplace.html does `const HIVE_ID = whHiveId()` once at load and stamps it on every hail and listing, so if the active hive could change while the page is open, work would be filed into the WRONG TENANT. It cannot today: the only pages that write `wh_active_hive_id` are hive.html (the switcher) and index.html (the sign-in bootstrap), and reaching the marketplace from either is a full page load, so the const is always read fresh. That was recorded as the A4 finding on `TB-A345-architecture-quality` — no defect — and it is a conclusion resting on an invariant nobody enforced: add an in-page hive switcher to the marketplace and every subsequent hail carries a stale tenant id with no test going red. Per this platform's disposition rule, a covered-by-nature cell still gets a gate asserting the contract it rests on. TWO ASSERTIONS: (A) the WRITER ALLOWLIST — exactly hive.html and index.html may write the key, and a third page appearing goes red with the instruction to re-check capture scope on every page that reads it, because adding a writer is a decision rather than automatically a bug; (B) THE CAPTURING PAGES MUST NOT WRITE IT — marketplace.html / marketplace-seller.html / marketplace-admin.html must contain zero writers, which is the live-bug condition, since a writer in the same document can run after the capture. CHECKING THE PREMISE CORRECTED THE FINDING TWICE, both errors mine: the cell claimed every write lives on hive.html (index.html:2953 writes it too — the conclusion survived, the stated premise was false), and index.html ALSO reads whHiveId() into a `const HIVE_ID`, which looks like the same stale-capture shape but is not, because that capture is FUNCTION-scoped inside the ops-home renderer (re-read per call) and the write is deliberately followed by `_initDashboard(...)` to re-render against the new hive — verified by reading both sites rather than trusting the comment. So the distinction that matters is SCOPE, not filename. The gate deliberately does NOT try to compute JS scope from a regex: brace and regex-literal counting over inline script is the brittle-validator trap this platform has already been bitten by, so it asserts the two cheap, unarguable properties instead. Self-test injects a writer into marketplace.html THROUGH THE READER (no file on disk is touched, the same discipline as injecting a mutant inside a transaction) and requires the gate to go red naming that page — without it, a green result would mean nothing. Static file scan, fast, always runs.

PAYMENT DISCLOSURE (§10 MK8) — while the platform holds no money, it must SAY so, AT the money step. WorkHive's marketplace is contact-only: PAYMENTS_ENABLED=false, no escrow, the buyer arranges payment with a stranger off-platform — so 100% of the money risk sits at one moment, the inquiry that takes the conversation off the site. RA 11967 (the PH Internet Transactions Act) requires consumer education on the red flags in internet transactions, and silence lets a buyer assume protection by default, because the default assumption everywhere else online is that the platform holds the money. TWO INVARIANTS: (1) the money step states that WorkHive NEVER HOLDS the payment, states the consequence (it therefore CANNOT REVERSE it), and gives a concrete precaution — 'payment is off-platform' states a fact but does not warn; (2) no buyer-facing copy promises buyer/purchase protection, a money-back guarantee, held funds or escrow — promises the switch makes false. Checked as CLAIMS rather than one exact sentence, so the wording stays free to improve while the substance may not quietly drop out. <script> and HTML comments are stripped first: a reassurance living in a comment reassures nobody. marketplace_orders DOES carry an escrow-shaped vocabulary (pending_payment/escrow_hold/released/refunded) for a flow that is switched off — fine as schema, which is why the gate searches PROSE and not status strings. SKIPS entirely if PAYMENTS_ENABLED flips to true: these invariants describe a different product then and must be re-derived, not silently kept. Self-test proves all four directions including the comment-only case.

LIFECYCLE STATE REACHABILITY (§10 MK4) — every state in a `status` CHECK must be both SURFACED and REACHABLE. A CHECK vocabulary is a promise about what the product does, and it breaks two ways, silently in both directions because unreachable code raises nothing. FOUND 2026-07-29: `marketplace_listings.sold` is fully dressed — a blue 'Sold' chip, a `.listing-item.sold` border rule, a schema.org/SoldOut mapping in the runtime JSON-LD, and `recompute_seller_sales_and_tier` COUNTS listings WHERE status='sold' to drive the seller's tier — and NOTHING anywhere writes it. A seller who sells something cannot say so, and the tier that counts sales counts a number that is always zero. (The mirror case is already recorded as a schema question for Ian: the same table carries moderation_reason/moderated_at/moderated_by with no `rejected` in its vocabulary — a consumer with no state.) THE PRODUCER TEST UNIONS THREE SIGNALS because none alone is right: the DERIVED guard matrix (a guard's allow-list only covers USER writes, missing `accepted` via the workhive.service_system_write bypass and `expired` via the sweep cron), a DB assignment (`SET status =` / `status :=` ONLY — matching `status = 'x'` anywhere counts WHERE-clause READS as writes, which produced a FALSE PASS on the one real finding twice in a row), and a page write including the literal passed as an ARGUMENT (the seller advances a job through `svcAdvance(id, next)`, so a payload-only test calls seven wired states unreachable). Forward-only: the known gap is NAMED in lifecycle_reachability_baseline.json and still prints every run; a NEW unreachable or invisible state FAILs. Self-test proves both baseline directions.

OFFLINE WRITE GUARD — a user-triggered write must REFUSE before it fires, not after. Found 2026-07-29 while building the test bank's S2-pwa cell: marketplace.html already had svcRequireOnline() ('You're offline. <action> needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.') wired into exactly TWO of its seven client writes. The other five fired into a dead network — svcSettle ('I paid', money, no idea whether it landed), svcApplyVoucher, svcPickQuote, svcPickStar, and svcClientCancel, whose confirm dialog made the person commit to cancelling before failing opaquely. marketplace-seller.html was worse: svcAccept reasoned about the offline race in a comment and the other NINE writes had nothing, including svcFileTopup where the provider may have ALREADY sent the GCash payment. WHY THE EXISTING GATES MISSED IT: degraded-state-central proves every page adopts the offline BANNER — and both pages did, the whole time; a passive warning does not stop a button. offline-queue-confirm proves a drain never calls 0 rows 'synced' — but these surfaces deliberately do NOT queue, because a queued accept would claim a job someone else already took. Adoption of a warning and correctness of a drain both passed while every individual write was unguarded. This gate asserts the third thing. Balanced-brace function extraction (not a fixed window), only user-invokable functions (window-attached or inline handler), read-only RPCs exempted BY NAME, and the check's POSITION is verified — a guard after the write is a post-mortem. Self-test proves all four directions including the order case.

C14 (SERVICE_HAILING_ROADMAP §4b) once-only on the money/dispatch paths. The roadmap originally asked for an `Idempotency-Key` header contract; reading the code first showed the platform already does something STRICTLY STRONGER — partial UNIQUE indexes enforce once-only in the DATABASE, so the guarantee holds even when the client sends no key, the wrong key, or is a script hitting PostgREST directly. 8 invariants: the four indexes exist (one commission per request · one top-up per GCash ref · one offer per provider+request · one open PM auto-hail) AND still BITE (a partial predicate can be narrowed to uselessness without dropping the index, so presence alone is not proof — each replay is attempted live in a rolled-back transaction and must be REFUSED), plus the duplicate must be reported HONESTLY ('That reference number is already filed'), never as raw 23505 text a user reads as failure and re-sends. Skips if docker/psql is absent.

C12 (SERVICE_HAILING_ROADMAP §4b) durable side-effects: a boundary-crossing effect must survive a consumer that is down. 12 live invariants over `service_outbox` + the `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` relay: schema/RLS/no-client-grant · enqueue+drain+reconcile are EXECUTE-revoked (a DEFINER helper is user-callable BY DEFAULT — this arc already shipped one live IDOR from that) · enqueue is a plain INSERT so it commits iff the transition does (an HTTP call inside the transition tx is the coupling the outbox removes) · a failed delivery is pushed OUT in time, not retried hot · a payload past max_attempts DEAD-LETTERS instead of looping · nothing is stranded 'in_flight' · SOMETHING ACTUALLY CALLS THE FAN-OUT · and a real enqueue→relay→2xx→done round-trip, minted and swept by the gate itself (residue is not evidence). WHY THE BLUNT ONES: Web Push shipped fully built and NEVER INVOKED — subscriptions, sw.js handler, VAPID, subscribe UI and notify-push all existed while no caller did, so providers subscribed and received nothing. 'Built but never called' must never be green again. Skips if docker/psql is absent.

P7 double-submit lock gate (static teeth) — every `getElementById('...').addEventListener('click', H)` bound to a WRITE handler H (name submit/save/confirm/create/add/send/publish/approve/reject/delete OR the body issues a `db.from().insert/upsert/update/delete` / `db.rpc` write) MUST be single-flight-locked, EITHER by wrapping the binding in `withButtonLock(this, H)` OR by H disabling its button before the await. A bare unlocked click->write binding = a double-tap fires the write TWICE (PRODUCTION_FIXES #47). REAL bugs locked 2026-07-21: inventory.html submitUse/submitRestock/submitPart (bare -> the non-idempotent inventory_deduct/restock RPC = a DOUBLE stock deduction) now wrapped in withButtonLock; logbook.html submitAsset (bare -> 2nd tap 23505s the (hive_id,tag) unique index) now self-disables. Read-only handlers (all db.from().select) + JS Set/Array .delete()/.update() are excluded (Map.size class). Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

DEEPWALK D3 gate (static teeth) — a list render that owns BOTH a first-run empty-state ('No entries yet — log your first X' CTA) AND a search no-results ('nothing matched your filters') must route a 0-result SEARCH to no-results, NEVER to the first-run empty-state. For a SERVER-filtered view (the list var IS the query result => `filtered === entries`) an early `if (entries.length === 0){ show empty-state; return }` fires FIRST and makes the no-results branch DEAD, so a supervisor who searched the whole TEAM feed and got 0 rows sees 'Log your first repair' (a nonsensical CTA). REAL bug found + fixed live 2026-07-22 in logbook.html renderEntries (the length-0 branch is now view-aware: team->no-results, mine->empty-state). Client-filtered views (inventory `filtered = items.filter(...)`) are correct and out of scope. Curated list of server-filtered search views; adding one is a conscious UX decision that must extend the gate. Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

DEEPWALK D5 gate (static teeth) — the 'number input's declared min/step/bounds are NOT enforced on the write path' class, across TWO central parsers. (a) QTY: a `<input type=number min=1 step=1>` in a modal that submits via a BUTTON (not a native <form>) never has min/step enforced; a bare `parseFloat()||0` lets 2.5 / 1e-9 through => a fractional/absurd stock deduction (inventory submitUse/submitRestock). (b) PRICE: the marketplace post/edit forms are `novalidate`, so min=0 is unenforced; an unvalidated negative hit the DB price_nonneg CHECK (raw 23514) and an over-precision value hit numeric(14,2) overflow, both cryptic to the seller (marketplace handlePostSubmit / marketplace-seller handleEditSubmit). REAL bugs found+fixed live 2026-07-22. FIX (central, METHOD LAW): window.whParseQty (integer qty) + window.whParsePrice (currency: blank=negotiable, 0=free, 2dp, ₱10M cap) in utils.js; every curated number-write handler adopts the right one. Gate locks: both helpers exist + window-exposed, every handler calls its helper, and none has a bare parseFloat/Number inline read (a naive revert). Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

DEEPWALK D2 gate (static teeth) — a NON-idempotent client write (a fresh-id INSERT or a decrement/increment RPC) has no idempotency key, so a refresh-mid-submit then retry creates a DUPLICATE / double effect (the button-lock only stops a same-page double-tap; a refresh spawns a fresh page that bypasses it). REAL, live-confirmed 2026-07-22: logbook addEntry (fresh Date.now() id => dup entry), inventory submitUse (inventory_deduct AGAIN => DOUBLE stock deduction), submitRestock (double restock), marketplace handlePostSubmit (dup listing). FIX (central, METHOD LAW): window.whRecentDuplicate(db, table, matchObj, {windowMs, tsColumn}) in utils.js queries for an identical recent row (tight window + specific match => no false-block; best-effort, never blocks a write on error); each handler calls it BEFORE the write and skips on a hit. Live-verified: retry dedups, different value not matched. Gate locks: the helper exists + window-exposed + every curated non-idempotent write calls it. Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

DEEPWALK D4 gate (static teeth) — a chat/message send that clears its input OPTIMISTICALLY (`input.value=''` BEFORE the async turn, to show the user bubble immediately) MUST restore it on the failure path, else a 429/timeout/network error WIPES the user's typed question even though the error says 'try again' (forcing a full retype). T123 (2026-08-28): whitespace must never decide whether the system works. People paste - a part number from a Viber message, a username from an email - and every pasted value can carry a leading or trailing space the person cannot see. Where the value is used for IDENTITY or MATCHING, that invisible character decides the outcome: a space on si-username/su-username and sign-in fails with correct credentials; a space in the inventory SEARCH and a part that exists returns nothing, which reads as 'we do not stock it' to someone standing at the shelf; a space in part_number/part_name on WRITE is baked into the record, so the row never matches its own search again; a space on a recipient email and the report bounces. All six are trimmed today and this holds them there. ★THE PROPERTY IS DELIBERATELY NOT 'TRIM EVERYTHING': dayplanner's note and logbook's knowledge field are textareas where a person may indent lines, so leading whitespace is CONTENT, and a gate demanding .trim() on every text field would enforce an opinion about prose and eventually be switched off. ★THE SCAN NEEDED CAREFUL READING, WHICH IS WHY THE SUBJECT LIST IS EXPLICIT: a search for untrimmed values reaching a payload flagged inventory's q and cat, both of which are the remembered-filter SNAPSHOT - restored into the input and re-trimmed at the point of use - so judging by the assignment rather than the use would have filed two defects against correct code. ★AND THE SELFTEST MUTATES COPIES, NEVER DISK: its first version rewrote the real product files and restored them in a finally block, which is one crash or one concurrent board read away from a corrupted source or a voided board. Selftest 7/7, each field mutated independently.

T4 (2026-08-28): a wall that promises to send you back must send you back, and only somewhere safe. An anon or hive-less visitor tapping into Community is bounced to the hive gate, and that bounce used to DROP the destination - so a person who set out for one place arrived somewhere else with no way back and nothing explaining why. Now community stamps hive.html?return=community.html and hive.html renders a 'Continue to Community' banner honouring it. TWO HALVES GATED TOGETHER because they are ONE promise in two files: a stamp nobody reads is a query string, a banner with nothing to read is dead markup, and a fix to either side alone breaks the promise with nothing erroring. ★THE THIRD CLAUSE MATTERS MOST - IT IS A SECURITY PROPERTY HIDING INSIDE A USABILITY FEATURE: ?return= is user-controllable, and the naive implementation (location.href = raw) is an OPEN REDIRECT, a link to our own trusted domain that lands the person on an attacker's page wearing our reputation. The guard must be a strict same-origin FILENAME allow-list, never a blocklist - one rejecting 'http://' and '//' still passes '/\evil.com' and a dozen encodings. Nothing about the feature LOOKS security-sensitive, which is exactly why its shape is locked. Fourth: the label is built with textContent, so a crafted filename cannot inject markup even if the allow-list is ever loosened. Selftest 6/6.

T134 (2026-08-28): a listing's photo leaves the public bucket when the listing does - and when it is REPLACED. Deleting a listing removed the row and left the JPEG at a permanent public URL, so 'this cannot be undone' was true of the row and quietly false of the photo: anyone holding the link still had it after the seller believed they had removed the listing. ★THE FIX-EVERY-PATH PASS FOUND THE BIGGER SOURCE - deleting is rare, REPLACING an image on edit is common, and it orphaned the old object exactly the same way, far more often. A gate holding only the delete path would have locked the half that almost never runs while the frequent one kept leaking, which is worse than no gate because the board would report the class closed. Holds both sites and both of the edit path's guards: remove only when the URL actually CHANGED (re-saving an unchanged listing must not delete its own live image) and only when the old object is OURS by bucket-marker (a seller may paste an external URL, and we must not reach into someone else's host). Both cleanups stay BEST-EFFORT and wrapped, running after the write so a storage hiccup can never cost the seller the edit or delete they asked for - the inverse of the coupling T12 had to break. Selftest 5/5. ★THE OWNERSHIP NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS FIRST: a whole-file search for indexOf(_marker) is satisfied by the DELETE path's own copy, so removing the EDIT path's guard left the file matching and the case passed while detecting nothing - two near-identical blocks on one page is precisely the shape that makes a loose check vacuous, and it is now scoped to the edit block.

It said 'we do not run third-party analytics... when we add web analytics in the future, this page will be updated' while GA4 (wh-ga4.js) was already live on 10 public pages. ★A STALE SENTENCE ON A LEGAL SURFACE IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF DEFECT: everywhere else drift means a number is wrong or a label is old, but here it means the document a regulator, an enterprise buyer or a worker reads to decide whether to trust us was making a FALSE STATEMENT about what we collect - false in the direction that flatters us, which is the direction nobody audits, and invisible because prose never looks broken. Comment-stripped, and that is not a formality here: the fix left an HTML comment quoting the old denial verbatim so the correction stays legible, and a detector reading comments would find 'when we add web analytics in the future' in the FIXED file and convict the page for documenting its own repair - the single most reliable false positive in this whole gate family, hit three times on other subjects this session. T12 (2026-08-28): a worker's note must outlive the AI that was going to answer it. voice-journal is where someone captures a thought mid-shift; the companion's reply is the nice part, the NOTE is the part that matters. ★THE ORIGINAL DESIGN LOST THE NOTE TO A QUOTA ERROR: the write happened server-side inside the voice-journal-agent call, so a 429 from the gateway meant the row was never written - the page was HONEST about it ('your note was not saved') and the note was still gone. Three clauses: (1) the page has its OWN EYES - noteLanded() re-reads for the note instead of inferring its fate from the call's outcome, because an error on the reply says nothing about whether the row exists and a page that guesses will tell a worker their words are gone when they are safe, or the reverse, which is worse; (2) it says the true sentence on BOTH paths - typed and spoken are separate catch blocks, so a fix landing in one produces a page that tells the truth depending on how you happened to enter the note; (3) the microphone failure NAMES ITS OWN CAUSE - one catch blamed 'permission denied' for every getUserMedia failure, so a mic-less desktop sent the worker to check a permission they never refused, and branching on err.name (NotAllowed/Security vs NotFound/Overconstrained) is the difference between a remedy and a wild goose chase, with every branch still naming the typed fallback.
