T144 (2026-08-28): acking a plant alert hides it for the WHOLE CREW, and the page must say so. alert-hub's dismissal is HIVE state - the upsert is keyed onConflict: 'hive_id,alert_key', NOT on the actor - so one person marking an alert handled removes it from every teammate's feed. That is deliberate: a plant alert is about a machine, not a personal inbox, and it should stop nagging the crew once somebody has dealt with it. ★IT IS ALSO THE ONE FAILURE MODE THIS PAGE CANNOT AFFORD IF IT HAPPENS SILENTLY - a worker tidying what they believe is their own view can blind the entire crew to a live plant condition - so the scope and the SENTENCE are held as ONE property: the write is hive-keyed; the row still records actor (crew-wide AND anonymous would be far worse than either alone); and the toast says both, 'hidden for your whole hive now, recorded under your name'. The old copy said only 'Alert marked handled', which is true and tells the person nothing about who else just stopped seeing it: a scope this wide is defensible when stated and indefensible when discovered. Also gates convergence - setInterval(loadAll, 60000) so a second tab is not stale forever, and a visibilitychange pause so a phone in a pocket is not polling a plant database with no reader. Selftest 6/6. ★ITS ATTRIBUTION NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS TWICE: a whole-file search for actor: WORKER_NAME also matched an UNRELATED upsert and two comments, so removing it from every dismissal still passed; and the mutation that fixed that deleted the upsert prefix too, tripping 'no upsert found' while the case was labelled 'losing attribution' - detecting something real and proving nothing about the clause it named. The mutation is now a named helper that removes ONLY the actor field, verified to leave the statement intact.

T9 (2026-08-28): a repair entry and its photo land together or not at all. The logbook is the platform's core write - a worker on a plant floor, one-handed, recording what they just fixed - and attaching a photo is where that write goes wrong on most systems, because a photo normally means a SECOND write (upload the file, then insert the row) and two writes have two ways to half-succeed: an orphaned file with no entry, or an entry claiming evidence it does not have. ★NEITHER IS REACHABLE HERE, BY CONSTRUCTION: logbook.html contains NO storage.from(...).upload() at all - the photo is compressed client-side and carried INLINE as a data URL in logbook.photo (a text column) inside the SAME insert as the entry, so there is no second write to fail. The decoupling T12 had to ARGUE for on voice-journal is free here. That is precisely why it needs a gate rather than a comment: adding an upload to this page would read as an IMPROVEMENT in review ('move photos to storage, keep rows small') and would silently reintroduce a failure class the page currently cannot have. ★THE COUPLING RUNS THE OTHER WAY AND IS THE REAL RISK - one row carries the typed work AND the image, so a big photo makes a big row and a failed insert takes the worker's words with it. Both halves gated: an oversize file is refused BY NAME before compression ('Photo too large (max 20 MB).') so the worker learns the limit instead of watching a save fail, and the image is compressed rather than sent raw. Fourth clause: when the AI vision path fails it must say the entry is UNCHANGED, because an analysis failure is not a save failure and a worker who cannot tell them apart retypes work that was never lost. Selftest 5/5, comment-stripped - this page documents its single-write design thoroughly, which is exactly what would let a prose-reading detector pass a file that had lost it.

T10 (2026-08-28): a task put off is not a task done. A worker who cannot do a PM today DEFERS it; one who does it COMPLETES it, and the gap between those is where a compliance percentage becomes a lie - if a deferral sets last_completed_at, next_due_date rolls forward, the item drops off the overdue list, and the plant's number rises for work nobody did. Nothing errors; the number just quietly stops meaning maintenance. ★THE ENFORCEMENT IS ONE CLAUSE IN ONE VIEW, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT NEEDS A GATE: v_pm_scope_items_truth's LATERAL join carries AND (pc.status = 'done'), so every consumer inherits the rule instead of re-implementing it - right design, and also a single dropped AND that would look like a harmless simplification in a diff. Three independent checks, because each can be true while another is false: STRUCTURAL (the view still carries the filter), EMPIRICAL (of the 5 scope items whose completions are ONLY deferrals, 0 carry a last_completed_at - structure can be right while a backfill or manual UPDATE made the data wrong), and LEXICAL (pm-scheduler's history still maps status to 'Completed'/'Deferred'). ★TWO OF MY OWN CUTS CONVICTED CORRECT CODE FIRST. I put analytics.html in the render list on the strength of this trajectory's own prose; analytics does NOT render PM status - its matches are comments about deferred CHART DRAWS and a deferred redirect. And I hunted raw-enum leaks with a regex, which flagged pm-scheduler's `status: isDefer ? 'skipped' : 'done'` - the DB WRITE. The enum SHOULD appear in code that talks to the database; what must never appear is the enum on the GLASS, so the check now reads the display ternary rather than pattern-matching a string with every right to be there. Fails CLOSED when the DB is unreachable. Teeth 2/2: rebuilds the view from its OWN definition with the predicate stripped, inside a rolled-back transaction.

T141 (2026-08-28): a fact about the NETWORK must not be rendered as a claim about PEOPLE. hive.html's presence bar answers 'who is here right now'; when the realtime link failed its fallback said 'Members offline' and painted every member with a solid offline dot - a positive claim about people made entirely from a fact about the websocket. Presence unavailable is NOT everyone-absent: the teammate you decide not to call may be standing at the machine. ★THE COST IS A DECISION, NOT A PIXEL - nobody reads a presence bar for fun, they read it to decide whether to walk over, phone someone, or handle it alone, and a bar that says 'offline' when it means 'I cannot see' sends that decision the wrong way while looking perfectly healthy. Same shape as a failed read rendering as an empty list, and it needs its own gate for the same reason: the honest state and the alarming state are both quiet. Four clauses - the fallback names the LINK; it asserts nothing about members being offline; the dot renders UNKNOWN (hollow fill with an outline) rather than the solid away-dot, because the dot is what people read at a glance; and both strings carry EN+FIL. ★THE FOURTH CLAUSE KEEPS THE OTHERS HONEST: renderPresence()'s genuine 'No one online yet' must stay DISTINCT, since that is TRUE when the link is UP and nobody is there - collapsing the two would trade this defect for its mirror image, reporting a real empty room as a network fault. Two notices, two truth conditions. Selftest 6/6, comment-stripped. ★ITS OWN FIRST RUN PRODUCED TWO CONFIDENT FALSE FINDINGS about correct code: find('function renderPresence') matches renderPresenceFallback, which is defined FIRST in the file, so the gate audited the fallback against the live path's rules. The lookup now requires the open paren - the same prefix-matching class as 'end' inside 'trend', caught only by the clean-file selftest case.

T170 (2026-08-28): a password arrives masked, and revealing it ANNOUNCES that it is revealed. Two halves, each useless alone. MASKED BY DEFAULT: every password field ships type=password, and the shared whPrompt honours inputType:'password' end to end - which had a real gap, since _mount read inputType but whPrompt built its own options object and never forwarded it, so a caller asking for a masked prompt silently got a plain text box and a secret was typed in the clear on a shared plant tablet. The caller was correct; the plumbing dropped it with nothing looking wrong. REVEAL MUST SPEAK: a show/hide toggle is a usability necessity because people mistype passwords on phones, but a control that silently changes whether a secret is visible is a shoulder-surfing hazard for exactly the person who cannot check by looking - so it must flip BOTH aria-label (what pressing it does next) and aria-pressed (what state it is in now). ★AND THE GATE ANCHORS ON THE ACCESSIBLE NAME RATHER THAN THE CODE SHAPE FOR A MEASURED REASON: a search for controls flipping an input type found ZERO, twice, because the pattern expected a quoted literal and togglePwd assigns a TERNARY. The three aria-labels reading 'Show password' were the only evidence the toggles existed - the accessible name was what the code-shape search could not see. Selftest 8/8.

T130 (2026-08-28): the longest LEGAL value must not break the form that accepts it. A maxlength tells a person how much they may type and says nothing about whether the layout survives them typing it - a field can advertise 200 characters and blow its container at 180, with nobody knowing until a worker with a long part number meets it on a phone. ★A RESTING SWEEP CANNOT SEE THIS, which is why the prover drives flows open: filling capped fields at rest reached 10 of 66, because the other 56 live inside modals, sheets, composers and wizard steps that do not exist until something is clicked - inventory, logbook, project-manager, community and pm-scheduler each reported ZERO capped fields, not for lack of caps but for lack of an opener. Reporting '66 fields, 0 break' off that run would have been a skipped partition reading as a covered one. The value is a single unbroken run of 'W' on purpose: a cap-length SENTENCE wraps and hides the overflow, while a cap-length part number, serial or URL - what people actually paste - does not. ★TWO OF MY OWN CUTS WENT GREEN OVER NOTHING BEFORE THIS WAS RIGHT. First, measuring geometry without visibility produced 18 'defects' that were one CLOSED feedback drawer (visibility:hidden at x=754 against a 390 viewport) counted once per page. Then, guessing the surface selector as '#part-form, #add-part-modal, form' when the real container is #part-modal reached 0 of inventory's 4 fields and reported ok - a prover that opens the right form and measures the wrong box is indistinguishable from a clean run. So each flow now declares how many fields it EXPECTS and under-reach is a FAILURE, not a quiet zero. 18 capped fields across 7 flows at 390, 0 breaking. Teeth 7/7: every flow with fields goes red when its container is widened, each verified clean=0 first. Read-only - fills, measures, restores; never submits.

T5 (2026-08-28): the action a person tapped BEFORE the wall must finish after it. An anon visitor taps Save on a listing; the platform answers with a sign-in door, correctly, and what decides whether the door was worth walking through is what happens on the far side. Returning them to the PAGE is the easy half and was already done; returning them to the ACTION is this one - toggleWatchlist's anon branch stashes wh_pending_action, loadWatchlist replays it once the person has a name. Proven live 2026-08-25 and then left with NO GATE, which is why this exists: the replay is four lines inside a loader, invisible to every other oracle, and its failure is SILENT - nothing errors, the listing is simply not saved, and only the person who tapped knows. Holds four clauses, each of which a plausible edit removes: the intent is stashed (in sessionStorage, so it dies with the tab - one that outlived the session would fire days later against a listing they no longer want); it is actually REPLAYED (a stash nobody reads does nothing); it is SINGLE-SHOT, the key consumed BEFORE the call so a throwing replay cannot loop; and it is IDEMPOTENT. ★THE LAST CLAUSE IS THE ONE WORTH GATING: the other three fail visibly the first time anyone walks the flow, but this one fires only when state raced ahead - saved in another tab, saved another way - and since toggleWatchlist is a TOGGLE, replaying over an already-saved listing UN-SAVES the very thing the person asked for. Its symptom reads as 'the platform lost my save', not as a replay bug. Selftest 7/7, comment-stripped because the fix's own comment describes all four clauses and a prose-reading detector would pass a file whose CODE had lost them.

T53 (2026-08-28): a person who only READS is never forced to write. Not every account operates the plant - a manager, an owner, a client on a site visit signs in to LOOK, reads, and leaves. That lane had no gate, because every existing journey asserts that an ACTION succeeds, and an action-shaped oracle cannot see this persona's defect: being stopped before reading anything at all. ★THE TRAJECTORY SPLITS AND ONLY HALF IS GATEABLE: whether the exec deserves a different LANDING is a design call and stays Ian's; whether a reader is FORCED INTO A WRITE is observable on arrival and needs no decision. Walks six exec-shaped surfaces signed in, settles, and requires no blocking modal, no body-scroll lock, no sign-in/pick-a-hive wall, no focus stolen into a text input (on a phone that opens a keyboard at someone who came to read), and no page error. ★THE SIXTH CLAUSE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, because the other five are all ABSENCES and a BLANK PAGE satisfies every one of them - an all-absence oracle grades a dead page as a perfect reading experience. So it also requires the reader actually got words, counting VISIBLE TEXT rather than figures: T53's own walk twice misread a healthy surface as thin, once by counting characters mid-render and once by counting figures on analytics-report, whose correct state is an instruction with no figures at all. The 220-char floor is deliberately low for exactly that page. Read-only by construction - never clicks, types or submits. 6/6 green at 1280. Teeth 5/5 via --teeth: each clause injected on a real signed-in page and asserted to fire, each checked non-vacuous (the clean page reported 0 first), because a gate locking already-correct behaviour has never been seen to go red and is otherwise a green light of unknown wiring.

CF: an optional API's absence must never hide CONTENT (T119, 2026-08-27). MEASURED by removing the capability an older engine lacks: index.html styled `.reveal { opacity: 0 }` and made those elements visible only when an IntersectionObserver callback added `.visible`, so on an engine without the API the constructor THREW, the rest of that script block never ran, and all 14 .reveal elements stayed invisible permanently - the landing page rendered 525 characters of text where every other page rendered 1146+. ★NOTHING WOULD HAVE REPORTED IT: no failed request, no error state, no blank shell - the page 'loaded fine' and simply never faded its content in, the same shape as a skeleton that never resolves. And the source SAID it was safe; the comment above the observer read 'all browsers', which is an assumption wearing the clothes of a check. ★THE GATE REQUIRES BOTH HALVES, because a guard alone is not enough: skipping the observer while leaving opacity:0 in place would pass a naive 'is it guarded' test and still ship a blank page. So every construction must have a feature check BEFORE it - positionally, since a check that runs after the throw protects nothing - AND the hidden class must have a reveal-everything fallback. Fixed at all five call sites, each failing OPEN: the main reveal shows everything, the stagger reuses its EXISTING reducedMotion branch rather than inventing a second path, the before/after rows are shown outright, and the sticky-CTA and nav-highlight observers (which only ADD behaviour) return early - the nav one was the loudest, constructing an observer PER SECTION. Verified both ways: without the API index renders 1061 chars and nothing throws; with it, .reveal still gains .visible on scroll. Teeth 4/4.

CF: a committing surface that holds TYPED work must be able to give it back (T38, 2026-08-27). A session dies, a phone is backgrounded, a tab is killed. On a page someone only READ, that costs a reload; on a page where they TYPED, it costs their words - and this platform's whole promise on a plant floor is that the work you did is the work that is recorded. So a page that both writes rows and offers a textarea must carry a draft mechanism. ★THE GATE'S OWN FIRST CENSUS WAS WRONG, WHICH IS WHY THE RULE IS SHAPED THIS WAY: checking for `whAutoSaveDraft` alone reported logbook.html - the flagship committing surface of the entire platform - as UNPROTECTED, when it has carried its own DRAFT_KEY / saveDraft / restoreDraft trio for months. Absence of the shared HELPER is not absence of the GUARD; a gate that recognises one implementation measures a naming convention, not the property, and would have sent someone to 'fix' a page that was already correct. Both forms count and a page is a finding only when NEITHER is present. MEASURED: 12 committing surfaces with typed work - 11 on the shared helper, logbook on its own, assistant exempt by reason (a chat turn is SENT immediately, so there is no compose-then-commit gap to lose) - and resume.html had NOTHING. Its #jd-input holds a job description the person PASTED from elsewhere, exactly the work that is expensive to reproduce: a session dying between the paste and the Tailor call sent them back to find the posting again. Fixed with the shared helper (which also stamps owner and age, so a shared plant tablet never hands one worker's paste to the next) and PROVEN LIVE - the paste survives a full reload byte-for-byte, restored into an empty field only. Teeth 4/4, including the one that matters: a page whose protection is page-local rather than shared must PASS.

CF: every success path of an XP-earning action must name the award (T17, 2026-08-27). MEASURED: a pm_completions insert pays XP through trg_pm_achievement, and submitCompletion() has TWO terminal success paths - one when the worker also mirrors the work to the logbook, one when they do not. The first announced ' · +N XP'; the second was SILENT. Same action, same trigger, same award, two different receipts, decided by an unrelated toggle ('also log this to the logbook') that has nothing to do with earning. That is the sibling-drift shape this codebase keeps meeting: a fix lands on the path someone walked and not the one beside it. ★SO THE RULE IS NOT 'THE PAGE MENTIONS XP SOMEWHERE' - it is that every success branch routes through ONE helper, because two inline copies would satisfy a mention-count check and drift again. ★AND THE RECEIPT READS THE LEDGER, NEVER RECOMPUTES IT: the trigger's rule lives in SQL (20 XP, +20 more for a detailed entry) and a JavaScript copy would be a second source of truth for a number shown to a worker as fact, so the helper reads achievement_xp_log back by source_id. Verified live that it is RLS-scoped: a row the signed-in worker owns returns ' · +60 XP', another worker's returns '' - so the receipt can neither leak nor overstate - and a failed read returns '' too, making it quieter but never wrong. The dedup-upgrade path is exempt BY REASON, not by silence: it turns a deferral into a completion with an UPDATE, and the trigger fires on INSERT, so no award is paid and claiming one would be inventing it. ★ITS OWN MATCHER WAS WRONG FIRST: a regex window stopping at the first ')' landed INSIDE the message text ('...Analytics (SMRP).') and reported two already-fixed paths as silent - a matcher that stops at a bracket the COPY happens to contain is measuring punctuation, not code - so it now scans balanced parens. Teeth 4/4: silent sibling, a helper that invents a number, a helper that counts reversed awards, and the clean surface.

CF: a printed artifact that shortens free text must SAY so (T49, 2026-08-27). export-reads-its-own-set holds the ROW axis - a CSV must not inherit the render buffer's cap, so no row goes missing. This holds the CELL axis on the same kind of artifact. MEASURED: project-report.html rendered every daily-progress log through `.slice(0, 200)` with nothing appended, and that page exists to be PRINTED and handed to a stakeholder. On paper there is no hover, no expand, no scroll - a 350-character blocker arrived as a complete-looking 200-character sentence, usually cut mid-word, and the reader had no way to know anything had been removed. Blockers is the field that carries WHY a project is late. ★THE RULE IS NOT 'NEVER TRUNCATE' - a printed column is real and text has to fit - IT IS 'TRUNCATE OUT LOUD': the cap stays, and a conditional marker plus a one-line table note now disclose it, appearing ONLY when the cap actually bites so a complete report carries no false alarm. Verified live on WO-2026-001: 6/6 rows render, zero marks and no note (no fixture value exceeds 200), while clip() on a synthetic 500-char value keeps exactly 200 and marks it, and a 50-char value passes through untouched. ★AND THE MARKER MUST REACH PAPER: a disclosure hidden by @media print discloses nothing to the person holding the printout, so that is asserted too. Proactive guard, teeth are synthetic negatives, 5/5: bare prose slice, unconditional helper, marker hidden in print, helper with no marker, and the real surface clean. One of those negatives initially replaced a string that did not exist in the source, so it tested the UNCHANGED file and passed vacuously - fixed to strip every marker token including the title attribute.

CF: a flow's OPENED state must fit the floor viewport, not just the page at rest (T113, 2026-08-27). ★THE GAP: control-within-viewport walks 16 pages AT REST, but the controls that decide whether work gets RECORDED do not exist at rest - the PM completion sheet, the deferral control, the add-task sheet are built or revealed mid-flow, and each is a different layout from the page hosting it. The resting sweep can be green over every page while the Save button of the sheet a worker must press sits off the edge: the same class T113 already found twice, one interaction deeper than any resting check can reach. Walks T10 (complete a PM, and its honest alternative - record a DEFERRAL) and T13 (the clock-in handover read) at 320. ★IT ARRIVES THE WAY A WORKER DOES: alert-hub hands pm-scheduler an ?asset=, the detail opens, and a REAL scope item's mark-done control is clicked. An earlier cut called openSheet() by hand and measured an EMPTY sheet - the same seven controls whatever the task, because markDone() is what fills in the item text, asset name, frequency badge and findings fields. That would have proved the sheet's chrome fits, not the sheet. ★AND A FLOW THAT NEVER OPENED IS REPORTED AS UNREACHED, NEVER AS CLEAN: the first run passed page.evaluate three arguments where it takes one, and every flow errored - counted as an instrument failure, which is why the run did not read as three tidy surfaces. Read-only: it opens and closes, never saves. ★AND FOR AN OVERLAY THE EDGE THAT MATTERS IS THE BOTTOM (T17 added 2026-08-27): the level-up card is a CENTRED FIXED overlay, so a card taller than a 320x844 phone puts its only dismiss button below the fold, and because the overlay does not scroll there is no gesture that reaches it - the reward moment becomes a trap. Driven through showLevelUpModal() with a REAL achievement id so the card carries its badge, heading and tier line, since an empty overlay is a different height. The bottom axis is checked only where a flow asks for it, because an ordinary PAGE is meant to extend past the fold - that is what scrolling is for - and flagging that everywhere would drown the finding. PROACTIVE guard (the property holds today), so its teeth are synthetic negatives, one per independent failure mode, all six verified: an off-screen control, a required control that is absent, a surface that does not exist, the real sheet clean at the floor, an off-BOTTOM control caught when the flow asks, and the bottom NOT checked when it does not - that last one proves the flag actually gates the check rather than being ignored. A width negative alone is NOT sufficient - at --width 200 the handover went RED while both PM sheets still passed.

CF: a flow's MESSAGES must speak the language the page is set to (T45, 2026-08-27). MEASURED: with wh_lang=fil, all three core field flows refused in English - logbook 'Please select an asset before saving.', pm-scheduler 'Please enter a task description.', voice-journal 'Write a note first, then send it.' ★WHY 100% FIL COVERAGE MISSED IT: the platform has TWO translation mechanisms and they cover different halves of the screen. data-i + whI18nApply swap STATIC markup at load - 442/442 here, which is where 'FIL is 100%' comes from - but every message the FLOW produces is born AFTER that pass, from showToast(...), which takes a raw string. The only translator that reaches those is _t(en, fil) at the call site. So the resting page was fully Filipino and the WORKING page was not, and no load-time DOM sweep can ever see it, because at load the message does not yet exist. ★THE EN CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT A MEASUREMENT: each step runs twice, fil and en, and only an identical multi-word message counts as untranslated - separating 'never translated' from 'same word in both languages'. ★AND AN EMPTY READING IS THE INSTRUMENT, NEVER A PASS: three earlier cuts of this prover scored a resting toast placeholder ('Entry saved.' is markup, not a message), a click that threw 'not visible', and a closed <details> whose hidden children still report layout rects - so the gate now refuses to grade any step it did not demonstrably reach. The steps are REFUSALS on empty required fields, so the walk writes no rows and needs no cleanup, and a refusal is the message a worker can least afford to not understand. Fixed by wrapping 14 call sites across the three flows, incl. a second inline refusal path for the same string. Resurrection-proved: the pre-fix logbook turns it RED (exit 1), the fix GREEN.

CF: a capped list must admit the rest exists (T129, 2026-08-27). A long list has to be capped - the DOM cannot carry two thousand rows and stay usable - so the danger is never the cap itself, it is a SILENT one: rows 1-20 of 548 rendered with nothing on screen admitting the other 528. That reads as 'this is everything', and a supervisor planning against it plans against a fifth of their own history. MEASURED at two volumes, which is what this holds in place: with the hive at 941 rows (314 for the signed-in worker) and again at 1641 (548), rows painted stayed 20 -> 20, DOM nodes 1458 -> 1396, first rows 1125ms -> 1221ms. A 75% growth in the reader's own history cost 96ms and NO dom weight, because the slice is constant - and the load-more wrap was offered rather than hidden, so the remainder was disclosed both times. THE PROPERTY IS THREE-PART because any one alone is not enough: the render must SLICE by a display count (or the page grows with the data), something must INCREASE that count (or the cap is a wall, not a page), and the control must be revealed exactly when more rows exist - toggle('hidden', count >= total). That third part is what makes the cap honest; without it a list can slice, own a hidden button, and still tell the reader nothing. Covers logbook and inventory, the two surfaces long enough to need it; teeth are a synthetic negative per part.

CF: the signup notice may only claim what was actually linked (2026-08-26). After creating an account index.html could announce 'Your existing records as <name> are now linked to your account' - and it decided that by COUNTING v_worker_truth rows matching the display name. That view exposes worker_profiles.display_name and is security_invoker, so under RLS a brand-new user can see exactly ONE row: the profile the very same flow inserted moments earlier. ★MEASURED on a fresh identity with no hive: c2_count = 1, visible_rows = 1 - so the count was always >= 1 and EVERY new signup was told their existing records had been linked. For someone who had none that is false; for a namesake it claims another person's work history, which is the same identity-by-name trap that let a second Juan Dela Cruz be refused a hive. ★THE CHECK AND THE ACTION READ DIFFERENT ROWS: the reassurance was computed from PROFILE rows while the actual linking is done by resolveActiveHiveContext(), which reads MEMBERSHIP. The notice now rests on that function's return value - non-null exactly when a membership was found and linked - and NAMES the hive it landed in, so the claim says what it rests on. ★THE GATE RUNS THE DB HALF LIVE rather than only reading the page, because the page assertion alone would not explain itself: it re-seeds a membership-less identity and re-measures the self-match, so if that count ever stops being 1 the gate says the PREMISE changed instead of passing quietly.

I-pillar: which hive a session is seated in is decided by AUTH, not by a name (2026-08-26). resolveActiveHiveContext() in index.html chooses the tenant a signed-in session lands in, and it selected memberships with .eq('worker_name', displayName) - where worker_name in v_worker_truth is worker_profiles.display_name. So the query asked 'which memberships belong to this NAME' and depended entirely on the profiles_read_own RLS policy (auth_uid = auth.uid()) to turn that into 'which memberships are MINE'. ★CORRECT, AND FOR THE WRONG REASON - which is the whole point: measured, a caller sees exactly ONE profile row, so the name filter could only ever match themselves and there was no live defect. But the safety lived in the POLICY, not in the query, and widening profile reads even slightly - a co-member roster is an ordinary thing to want - would have let a NAMESAKE's memberships resolve here and seated a person in a hive they do not belong to. The view already joins membership on hm.auth_uid = wp.auth_uid, so the name filter bought nothing the identity does not buy more safely. Verified no behaviour change on a real multi-hive account: both filters return the same two memberships. ★THIS IS THE THIRD FACE OF ONE DEFECT, all found the same day: a hive join that refused a second Juan Dela Cruz by unique index, a signup notice that counted its own freshly-written profile row, and a tenant seat chosen by name. A name is not an identity. ★BOTH HALVES ARE ASSERTED because either can rot: the page must filter by identity AND worker_profiles SELECT must still be self-scoped - if that policy widens, the gate says so rather than passing quietly, since that widening is precisely what would have made the old code dangerous. An unknown identity must mean SOLO MODE, never a name guess. Teeth: reverting the filter to worker_name goes RED on both assertions.

T185/security: the one credential that admits a stranger to a plant (2026-08-26). A hive's 6-character invite code is the whole of what stands between an outsider and a plant's maintenance records - hand it over and you are in - and it was generated with Math.random(), a plain PRNG whose internal state is recoverable from a handful of observed outputs, making later codes from the same page predictable. There was no compatibility excuse: createHive already REQUIRES crypto.randomUUID() (a null id aborts the create), so the page depended on modern crypto two lines away. ★THE CENSUS IS WHY THIS GATE IS NARROW AND NOT A BAN: 31 Math.random() uses across the production pages and exactly ONE was a credential - the rest are element ids, upload filenames, retry jitter and an analytics session id that already prefers randomUUID, all cases where collision resistance matters and unpredictability does not. Banning Math.random outright would have raised 30 false findings and taught everyone to ignore the gate. ★IT ALSO GUARDS THE MODULO, the part a future editor breaks silently: mapping random bytes with `b % len` is unbiased ONLY when len divides 256. The alphabet is 32 characters (O/0/I/1 omitted so a code survives being read aloud in a noisy plant) and 256 % 32 = 0, so each character gets exactly 8 byte values; add one character for readability and the first 256 % len characters quietly become likelier. The gate COMPUTES that rather than trusting it - teeth-proven by a 30-character alphabet, which it caught as favouring the first 16. ★COLLISIONS WERE ALREADY SAFE and were checked before being claimed: hives carries UNIQUE (invite_code), so a repeat is a clean create failure routed through whWriteError ('Nothing was made; try again'), never a cross-tenant join into the wrong plant.

T8: re-authenticating costs one sign-in, not your place (2026-08-26). When a token expires, session-timeout.js sends the worker to index.html?signin=1&return=<where they were>, and index.html validates that value before honouring it - an open-redirect guard, and the right instinct. But the guard's character class did not include characters the platform's OWN pages write into their URLs. ★MEASURED BY ROUND-TRIPPING THE REAL CHAIN (page writes filter -> session-timeout captures -> index re-reads): URLSearchParams.set() encodes a space as '+', and audit-log.html mirrors its filters into the URL including `actor`, which is a worker's NAME - so `audit-log.html?actor=Leandro+Marquez` and `audit-log.html?q=pump+seal` both failed the guard and were dropped IN SILENCE, landing the supervisor on the dashboard. That is T28's exact scenario, someone mid-investigation into who changed what, losing their place to a token refresh with nothing on screen explaining why. ★WHY WIDENING TO + , : IS SAFE, ARGUED NOT ASSUMED: the guard's job is to refuse a scheme, a protocol-relative //, and a foreign absolute path, and its ANCHOR already requires the value to begin with <name>.html or /workhive/ - so those three can only appear AFTER the ? or #, where a colon cannot read as a scheme and a plus is just a space. The gate proves both halves rather than trusting the argument: 8 real destinations survive AND 10 attack shapes (javascript:, //evil.com, https://, ../../, backslash-UNC, index.html@evil.com) are still refused. ★IT EXTRACTS THE REGEX FROM index.html instead of restating it, because a gate holding its own copy proves only that the copy is fine - and it FAILS IF THE THREE GUARDS DISAGREE (sign-in, signup, entry bridge), since a fix reaching one path and not the others is how this class survives. Teeth proven on both: the pre-fix class resurrects the two dropped destinations, and reverting a SINGLE guard is caught as disagreement.

T8: the sign-in screen says WHY the worker is looking at it (2026-08-26). A worker mid-task looks up and finds a sign-in modal with no explanation, which is indistinguishable from being logged out at random - and the question in their head goes unanswered: did I lose what I was doing? ★ONE FUNCTION, THREE EVENTS, THREE DIFFERENT TRUTHS: session-timeout.js's clearIdentityHard() runs for an automatic idle timeout, for the worker deliberately pressing Sign out, AND (via the storage listener) for a sign-out in another tab. Telling someone who just pressed Sign out that their session 'timed out' is false, so the reason is now a parameter, the deliberate path passes none, and the gate asserts that separation - collapsing it is the easy mistake, and passing clearIdentityHard straight to addEventListener would make the click EVENT the reason. ★THE REAL ASSERTION IS THE CLAIM'S PRECONDITION, NOT THE WORDING: the notice tells an idle-timed-out worker 'your drafts are still here', which is true ONLY because clearIdentityHard wipes identity keys alone (wh_last_worker + the hive keys) and never touches whAutoSaveDraft storage. Add a draft key to that wipe list and the copy silently becomes a lie no test would catch - so the gate READS the wipe list and fails on anything draft-shaped. A claim has to rest on something; this is the something. ★AND THE COPY IS A WHITELIST, NOT INTERPOLATION: ?reason= comes from the URL, so it is looked up in a fixed table and written with textContent, and an unknown value renders NOTHING - verified live across four cases (idle and othertab show; a deliberate sign-in and a nonsense reason stay silent). role=status so a screen-reader user is told too. Teeth proven on all three.

T129/T49: the file that leaves the building must be complete (2026-08-26). A logbook export is what an auditor reads, and it is the one artifact whose incompleteness the reader CANNOT see: a short LIST shows a Load more button, but a CSV carries no total, no window and no hint of omission. ★THE RECORDED INCIDENT: the team-branch export handed over `_teamEntries` - only what the feed had fetched, one 30-row page plus whatever Load more added - while the page said '517 entries'. A supervisor exporting a filtered team view for a DOLE/ISO trail got a file that looked whole. The mine branch had been fixed in an earlier arc; the team branch was the one nobody had walked. ★THREE ASSERTIONS: every exporter reads its OWN set by PAGING (a loop with .range) rather than reusing the render buffer, since an export sourced from a screen buffer inherits that buffer's cap; the paging carries a TOTAL order (sort key AND tiebreak), because a non-total order over a paged read can repeat one row and drop another - a file of the right LENGTH and the wrong CONTENTS, worse than a short one; and the property is NON-VACUOUS, checked against the database (largest hive 1,700 rows against a 30-row page) so it cannot pass on a table too small to fail. ★IT NAMES THE BUFFER IT FORBIDS rather than pattern-matching 'looks like an export', because the bug was one identifier. ★AND ITS FIRST VERSION MADE TWO FALSE ACCUSATIONS: a fixed 4000-character window ran past the function's end, through the next one and into the click handler, so it reported BOTH exporters as reusing the feed buffer when neither does - one hit was a COMMENT describing the old bug, the other the handler's ANNOUNCED fallback (which is correct behaviour: it exports the loaded window and says so in a toast). Bodies are now delimited by matching braces. A window sized to today's code is wrong the day someone documents something. Teeth proven on both the buffer reuse and a missing tiebreak.

T124: the printed page must not be the dark theme (2026-08-26). Plants run on paper - a PM schedule goes on the noticeboard, an audit trail into a folder for DOLE - and this platform is DARK. Printed without rules that is either a black sheet that empties a cartridge or, because most browsers drop backgrounds, pale grey text nobody can read. Neither failure appears anywhere ON SCREEN, which is exactly why it needs a gate: print CSS is invisible until it has already wasted someone's trip to the printer. MEASURED: the three pages a plant demonstrably prints already do this properly - white sheet, #111 text, the reset applied to DESCENDANTS (each card and chip carries its own dark background, so a rule on body alone leaves them), the hub/FAB/toasts/dialogs/buttons hidden, and page-break-inside on cards and table rows. This is a RATCHET over work already done, and the held set may not SHRINK - deleting the rules is not a way to pass. ★ITS FIRST VERSION MANUFACTURED FIVE FINDINGS AND ALL FIVE WERE WRONG, which is the part worth keeping: (1) it treated every @media print block as a claim to be printable, but asset-hub's block says in its own comment that it exists so the rule is 'reachable from document.styleSheets' for a DIFFERENT gate, and the report pages already render as light document panels where a dark-to-light reset would be redundant; (2) it read only the FIRST print block, and analytics-report carries SIX - the first being a one-line rule about a field's min-height - so five pages were graded on whichever rule sorted earliest; (3) its skip-list matched substrings against the ABSOLUTE path, and this project lives under '.../Self-learning Road-Map/...', which contains 'learn' - so it excluded EVERY page and reported '0 printable pages examined' while still failing. Three instrument errors before one true reading. ★AND ITS PASS LINE OVERSTATED until corrected: it claimed all 8 pages met the contract when only 3 are held. Teeth proven on a weakened rule AND on deletion.

T20: a refusal must reach the person who was refused (2026-08-26). A supervisor clearing the approval queue rejects an asset, a part, a change order; the item leaves the queue and their job is done - but the WORKER who submitted it is the one who has to act, and if all they ever see is 'Rejected' they resubmit the same thing, give up, or go and ask in person. A refusal that names no cause is a loop the platform opened and did not close. ★BOTH HALVES ARE ASSERTED because either alone is useless: every path writing status 'rejected' records a REASON in the SAME update (a reason captured later, or optionally, is a reason usually missing), and every surface that knows about the rejected state RENDERS it back (a column written and never read is the write-only class, and the submitter is the only person it was written for). ★IT PAIRS WRITES TO RENDERS BY TABLE, NOT BY PAGE, because the halves deliberately live apart: the supervisor rejects from hive.html and the worker reads the reason on inventory.html - a check demanding both in one file would fail the working design. MEASURED: all three paths already comply (hive's queue for asset_nodes AND inventory_items, asset-hub's own reject, project-manager's change orders), rendered as 'Why: ...', 'Why rejected: ... - fix it and resubmit via Edit', and 'Rejected: ...' - and asset-hub even says 'No reason recorded.' for rows predating the column rather than showing an empty box. Nothing was broken; nothing was guarding it, and a fourth reject path added later would have no reason to know the contract exists. ★ITS OWN FIRST RUN WRONGLY ACCUSED asset-hub, by matching a capitalised 'Rejected' caption when that page branches on `status === 'rejected'` inside a template - the state is a VALUE there, not a caption. Teeth proven on both halves.

T21: scheduling a PM must not lose the asset (2026-08-26). A supervisor approves a new asset and the next thing they do is give it a maintenance program. If the link carries the asset that is one tap; if it does not, they arrive at a list of everything and have to re-find the asset they were just looking at - which on a phone, in a plant, is where the task gets abandoned. ★BOTH ENDS ARE ASSERTED, because a parameter nobody reads is a promise only the sender believes it is keeping - the declared-but-never-wired class: every pm-scheduler link rendered with an ASSET in hand carries its identity (?tag / ?asset / ?asset_id), AND pm-scheduler actually consumes them (it reads all four: asset_id, asset, pm_id, tag). ★EMPTY-STATE LINKS ARE EXEMPT AND IT IS NOT A LOOPHOLE: asset-hub's two bare links both sit under 'No approved assets in this hive yet', where there is no asset to name and demanding a parameter would be demanding a lie - and the exemption is decided by the surrounding TEXT, not by an allowlist a later edit could quietly join. MEASURED: 2 links carry the asset, 2 are bare in genuine empty states. ★ITS FIRST RUN ACCUSED A COMMENT - 'Canonical PM frequencies (match pm-scheduler.html's FREQ registry)' - because it matched the bare filename anywhere; a mention is not a navigation, so it now matches only href= and .href= assignments. Teeth proven by dropping the asset from a real link.

T24: a reported post must not vanish on the person who wrote it (2026-08-26). When a teammate reports a post the platform hides it from the hive until a supervisor rules, and the easy way to build that is ONE predicate - hide every flagged post from every worker - which is wrong for exactly one person: the AUTHOR, who wrote something, watched it disappear, and was told nothing. They re-post it or conclude the app is broken, and either way the moderation nobody has done yet has already cost their trust. ★THREE PARTIES, THREE OBLIGATIONS: the author keeps seeing their OWN flagged post (the feed query must EXEMPT their rows, not merely filter flagged=false); the author is TOLD in words what happened, who decides, and that teammates cannot see it meanwhile (a post that reappears unexplained is barely better than one that vanished); and the SUPERVISOR sees the REPORTER'S REASON on the card, because judging a flag without knowing why it was raised means opening the audit log first, and a queue that costs a tab is a queue that waits. ★IT CHECKS THE QUERY PREDICATE, NOT JUST THE BADGE, and that is the half a page-level check would miss entirely: if the row is filtered out server-side the badge is unreachable, so the render can be perfectly correct while the author still never sees their post. MEASURED: all three hold today - the author exemption, the UNDER REVIEW state carrying its explanation, and the reporter's reason inline for the supervisor. Teeth proven on the predicate and on the notice.

T95: a bookmark must not imply a subscription (2026-08-26). Tapping a star on a listing looks like 'tell me when this changes'. Here it is a BOOKMARK - nothing consumes marketplace_watchlist to send price or stock alerts - and a buyer who believes otherwise STOPS CHECKING the listing and misses the very change they were watching for. The feature would do harm precisely by seeming to work. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY HANDLES THIS WELL, which is why this is a PARITY check and not a defect report: marketplace.html says outright "WorkHive doesn't send watchlist alerts yet." Stating an absence plainly is the honest answer to a capability you have not built. ★AND IT IS ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which most claim-checks are not: while nothing consumes the watchlist the disclosure must be PRESENT (deleting the sentence silently restores the implied promise), and once something DOES consume it the disclosure must GO - a stale 'doesn't send alerts yet' under a feature that now sends them is the same defect pointing the other way, and it teaches people to ignore the one place the product tells them the truth. A claim and a capability drift apart in either direction; a gate watching only one of them is half a gate. ★A CONSUMER MEANS AN EDGE FUNCTION OR CRON, not a page reading its own list to draw stars - the distinction is what stops the gate flipping on the rendering code. Teeth proven BOTH ways: deleting the sentence, and adding a function that touches the table.

T77/T164: the most private surface must say what you can take back (2026-08-27). A worker speaks or types something personal into the voice journal, and two facts govern whether they should - neither guessable. THE NOTE IS PERMANENT: ai-gateway persists the row inside the same call that generates the reply, so it exists before the worker has seen anything, and renderHistory's only per-entry action is 'Speak again' - no edit, no per-note delete. AND THERE IS SOMEWHERE TO GO: the privacy policy's Data Rights Request route, which validate_erasure_path_intact already proves the database honours. ★THE IN-APP ERASURE IS VOICE-ONLY AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT ADVERTISED AS THE REMEDY - the gate FAILS if the page starts offering it. voice-handler's _isErasureRequest does detect 'delete my voice history', but it is reached from _onStopRecording alone, so only after a voice recording; this page's typed fallback exists, in its own words, for 'a loud plant floor, a denied mic, or a worker who cannot speak', and pointing those people at a spoken phrase offers a remedy that excludes precisely whoever most needs it. ★AND IT ASSERTS THE DISCLOSURE APPEARS ONCE, because the first attempt at this fix was DUPLICATION: the permanence was ALREADY stated on the primary surface, and a new paragraph restating it landed inside a collapsed <details> nobody opens - a second home for information that already had one. Reverted; the fix became a single clause completing the sentence that was already there. Teeth proven on the missing route and on the duplicate.

T38: typed work must outlive a session expiry (2026-08-27). A worker half-fills a logbook entry, the token dies, they sign in again - and whether their typing is still there depends on a three-link chain no single file makes visible, with every link in a different place: whAutoSaveDraft persists the text; session-timeout's clearIdentityHard wipes the IDENTITY keys and must not touch draft keys; and the draft is restored only to the worker who typed it, by an OWNER CHECK that reads wh_last_worker - the very key the expiry just deleted. ★SO THE DRAFT SURVIVES ONLY BECAUSE RE-AUTH PUTS THAT KEY BACK. Sign-in rewrites wh_last_worker, so by the time the worker returns the owner check matches again and the text reappears. Re-key that check to something sign-in does NOT restore and every draft on the platform is silently discarded after an expiry: the form comes back empty and nothing explains it. That is the assertion - the key the owner check reads must be one the sign-in path writes. ★THE OWNER CHECK IS NOT THE BUG, it is the shared-tablet protection: worker A's draft must not appear in worker B's form. Removing it would 'fix' the expiry case by leaking someone's typing to the next person on the device, which is worse. ★AND THE ASSERTION HAD TO BE 'AT LEAST ONE LINK', NOT 'EVERY LINK': the check is a fallback chain (wh_last_worker || wh_worker_name) and utils.js records that the alias reads are dead - 'never written anywhere in the codebase (get-without-set)'. Demanding every link be restored flagged that dead alias and called a working chain broken. Teeth proven on both clauses: sign-in ceasing to restore the key, and an expiry that starts wiping a draft key.

T101: 100% of the money risk sits at one step (2026-08-27). This is a CONTACT-ONLY marketplace - no escrow, no held funds, no reversal - so a buyer contacts a stranger and pays them off-platform, and every peso of risk lives at that single moment. RA 11967, the PH Internet Transactions Act, requires consumer education on the red flags in internet transactions, which makes this a legal floor as well as a decent one. ★STATING A FACT IS NOT WARNING: 'payment is off-platform' is true and tells a buyer nothing about what to DO. The page carries an actual warning at the decision point - inspect the item, meet at the seller's business address or a public place, avoid paying in full up front to a new seller - and the sentence that sets expectations correctly: WorkHive never holds your payment, so we cannot reverse it. ★THE OPPOSITE FAILURE IS WORSE THAN SILENCE, so the gate also refuses escrow / buyer-protection / money-back / guaranteed-refund language on the marketplace surfaces: a buyer who believes there is protection behaves as though a loss is recoverable. It strips COMMENTS before matching, so prose ABOUT a promise is not read as the promise. ★AND IT HOLDS TWO SUBTLE CLAIMS THE PAGE ALREADY GOT RIGHT: 'credits back' must carry that credits are spend-only and cannot be withdrawn, because the bare words read like money returning; and the trust bar must say 'ID-Verified badge per seller' rather than 'ID-Verified Sellers', which as a bare heading reads as a property of the RESULTS - the same false claim the source chip carried when 3 of 9 listings actually had a verified seller. Teeth proven on the removed reversal sentence and on an introduced protection promise.

T71: the page that reports the outage must load during it (2026-08-27). whReadError sends a person to status.html when a read fails on good internet, because 'is it me or them?' is the one question a failure state can actually answer - and that pointer is only honest if the status page works when the platform does not. ★TWO WAYS A STATUS PAGE LIES, and both are asserted: (1) IT DEPENDS ON WHAT IT REPORTS - a page that needs the database cannot report a database outage; it fails exactly when someone finally needs it, and the reader concludes the whole product is gone. So status.html must carry no Supabase client, no getDb, no table read. (2) IT IS HARDCODED GREEN - 'All systems operational' baked into the markup is a trust signal with no living producer: it stays green THROUGH the outage and is worse than no page at all, because it actively contradicts what the person is experiencing. ★WHAT IT DOES INSTEAD IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, and the measurement confirms it: no database reference anywhere, and it pings each edge function's public /health endpoint, rendering one card per service, ambering when a round-trip exceeds the interactive SLO, with a Refresh to re-check. Live per service, independent of the database - which is precisely why it can still answer when the database is the thing that is down. ★IT ALSO HOLDS THE POINTER ITSELF: if utils.js stops sending a failed read to status.html, every failure state goes back to answering 'is it me or them?' with silence. Teeth proven on both lies - a Supabase client introduced, and a hardcoded green.

T28: an audit nobody can reach is write-only (2026-08-27). 'Who changed this?' is asked while looking at the RECORD - an asset whose details are wrong, a reported post, a decision someone disputes. If the only way in is to know the page exists and open it cold, the trail is technically complete and practically useless: the supervisor gives up or goes to SQL, and the compliance story the platform tells about itself is one nobody can walk. ★A LINK THAT DROPS THE RECORD IS BARELY BETTER - arriving at an unfiltered log of every power action while holding the id in your head is the same scavenger hunt with extra steps. So BOTH ends are asserted: the links must carry the subject (asset-hub sends ?q=<tag>, community sends ?action=report_post) AND audit-log must CONSUME those parameters, or the context is written into the URL and thrown away - a promise only the sender believes, which is the declared-but-never-wired class. MEASURED: two context-carrying links, audit-log consumes all four of q/actor/action/target. ★THE HIVE MENU ENTRY DOES NOT SATISFY THIS: audit-log is a hidden page, so a menu item makes it reachable only to someone who already knows to look; the record-level affordances are what make it findable at the moment the question is actually asked, which is why bare links are reported but do not count toward the requirement. Teeth proven on both halves - links stripped of their record, and the audit page ceasing to read what it is sent.

T25: being removed from a hive must not arrive as an empty screen (2026-08-27). A supervisor kicks someone; the supervisor's side is a confirm and a roster that shrinks. The WORKER's side is the one that matters - they open the app and their hive is simply gone, and without a word the honest readings available to them are 'the app broke' and 'my work was deleted', one of which is frightening enough to end their use of the product. ★THREE THINGS A REMOVED PERSON NEEDS, all asserted: WHAT HAPPENED (removed from the named hive, BY A SUPERVISOR - without an actor it reads as a malfunction), WHAT SURVIVED ('your personal records are still yours', which is the fear underneath, and silence about it is read as loss), and WHAT NOW (join another hive or create one - otherwise the notice tells someone their place is gone and leaves them there). ★AND IT MUST BE HELD LONG ENOUGH TO READ, which is the part usually missed and is asserted as part of the disclosure rather than as styling: the page's toast hides at a fixed 3s and this notice overrides it to 12s. Three seconds is fine for 'saved'; it is not enough for two sentences about your identity and your work, and a message nobody finishes reading was not delivered - the zero-millisecond-refusal lesson wearing a longer coat. Teeth proven on the hold (dropped to 2.5s) and on the records reassurance (removed).

T3/T154: the markdown twin must say what the page says (2026-08-27). Every public page ships a clean twin at <page>.md - the llms.txt convention, served deliberately (_headers: 'Markdown twins ... every page also exists at <page>.md') so answer engines read structured text instead of scraping markup. That makes the twin a PUBLISHING CHANNEL, and a stale one is worse than none: an agent fetching it gets a confident, well-formed, WRONG version of the page. ★MEASURED 2026-08-27: 107 of 119 twins had DRIFTED, including privacy-policy and terms-of-service - an answer engine could quote retired legal text. The sharpest instance was T3's recorded defect surviving in the machine channel after being fixed in the human one: 60 calculator twins still said 'free, no sign-up needed' on a link INTO engineering-design.html, which redirects to sign-in, while the HTML had already been corrected to 'A free account takes about 30 seconds'. Zero served pages carried the claim; sixty twins did. ★THE VALIDATOR ALREADY EXISTED AND WORKED - tools/validate_md_twins.py, with a source_sha per twin and the right reasoning in its own docstring - and NOTHING RAN IT: it appeared in no gate registration, the same orphaned-prover shape as the three unreferenced provers found earlier this session. A working oracle nobody runs is indistinguishable from one never written. Fixed by rebuilding (118 rebuilt, 119/119 current, 0 twins still carrying the claim) and by REGISTERING the validator, so the next HTML edit that forgets the twin fails here instead of shipping a confident wrong answer to a machine. FIX ON FAIL: python tools/build_md_twins.py. ★NOW IN --fast (2026-09-11): registering the gate was only half the repair - it was registered skip_if_fast, and the discipline this project actually runs is '--fast at milestones, the full board is Ian's ~6h gate'. So this gate was structurally unrun for the ENTIRE duration of every edit wave, which is precisely when twin drift is created. Measured today: one card blurb on learn/index sent me into the generated mirror, and the rebuild reported 117 of 120 twins ALREADY DRIFTED from the day's earlier edits - 117 public pages serving a confident, well-formed, wrong copy of themselves to answer engines, with no milestone check able to see it. The validator costs 1.98s. skip_if_fast is for expensive gates; a 2-second check guarding a PUBLISHING CHANNEL earns nothing by being skipped and loses a whole wave of visibility. A registered gate that never runs in the mode you actually run is the orphaned-prover shape one layer up - [[feedback_three_ways_a_lock_is_hollow]].

UFAI experience-in-motion source-grep dims (2026-07-22, PDDA_UX_PAINPOINT_JOURNEY_ROADMAP) — the 3 journey dims the runtime __RUBRIC lens can't cleanly see, measured from page SOURCE + forward-ratcheted: J3 consequence (every destructive handler routes through the shared whConfirm OR is soft-delete-undoable — NN/g 'undo > confirmation'), G5 system-memory (a filterable page persists the user's filter/view/sort choice to localStorage), S4 behavioral-consistency (destructive actions use the ONE shared whConfirm, no raw window.confirm). Emits journey_ux_dims_report.json (the coverage-gate source for J3/G5/S4). Baselines in journey_ux_dims_baseline.json ratchet forward. Self-test: --selftest.

The fix is a set of SHARED rules in tokens.css (the ONE file every page loads): input.wh-input/select.wh-select 44px, .btn-secondary/.btn-ghost 44px, img{max-width:100%}. This static gate asserts those shared rules STAY — remove one and every form control / secondary button / image on every page silently regresses below the field standard. Forward-only. Authority-link resolution (V3 5, AIO: every outbound citation still resolves; 404/410 = dead and ratcheted, bot-challenge 403 = shielded and reported, never failed). ★NOW IN --fast, AND IT NOW READS BARE TEXT (2026-09-21, W46181). This gate was registered skip_if_fast, and '--fast at milestones, the full board is Ian's ~6h gate' is the discipline this project actually runs - so it was structurally unrun for the entire duration of every edit wave, which is exactly when a citation rots. COST, measured twice and stated as a RANGE because it is network-bound, not CPU-bound: 13.7s direct with warm connections, 58.7s through the registry on a cold one - it fetches ~18 third-party URLs with a 12s timeout each, so a slow or shielded host dominates it. Same repair as md-twins-current, same reasoning: a check guarding a PUBLISHING CHANNEL must run in the mode you actually run. FIX ON FAIL: open the page and either correct the URL or remove the claim the dead source was carrying - a claim whose only citation 404s is a claim with no source.

This comparison is REVIEWED QUARTERLY for pricing and feature accuracy' — and NOTHING ENFORCED EITHER the date or the cadence. The failure mode is specific: a competitor raises its price, our page keeps quoting the old one, and a comparison that was accurate when written becomes a misleading claim about another company's product — worse to be wrong about than our own. The gate parses each page's own stated date and cadence and fails when the page outlives its own promise, or when a named vendor's price carries no date at all. ★SCOPE IS PROXIMITY, NOT CO-OCCURRENCE, and that was learned the hard way: the first version scoped in any page where a brand appeared anywhere and a price appeared anywhere, and immediately produced a FALSE POSITIVE — the platform guide names Fiix as an INTEGRATION TARGET in one table row and quotes a generic 'often around $20 to $50 per user per month' in another, and neither is a claim about Fiix's price. AH7 - a severity-9 failure mode must never be buried by RPN. The RPN arithmetic was already sound (rpn is a GENERATED ALWAYS column S x O x D, inputs CHECK-bounded 1..10, 0 of 300 rows disagreeing) - the defect was what the page DID with it: every FMEA surface ordered by rpn DESC alone, and because RPN multiplies severity by how RARE and how DETECTABLE a failure is, a rare easily-caught SAFETY failure scores below a frequent nuisance. Measured: all 17 modes with severity >= 9 sat below the median RPN, and 'Cable insulation breakdown' (S9, safety, RPN 108) ranked BELOW 'Coupling misalignment beyond 0.05 mm' (S6, production, RPN 180) on every asset page and every printed report - a report whose own header cites AIAG-VDA 2019, the standard that replaced RPN precisely because of this. canonical/standards.json had already recorded the caveat; the UI sorted by RPN anyway. Fixed with an Action Priority band (severity >= 9 or RPN >= 200 -> H; severity >= 7 or RPN >= 100 -> M) that only ever RAISES priority, so nothing urgent today is quietly demoted, registered as a PARTIAL formula variant because it is the severity escalation both IEC 60812:2018 and AIAG-VDA agree on and NOT the full ~1000-cell AP lookup - inventing that table's contents would defeat the point of an auditable contract. Holds: the helpers exist, BOTH the screen and the printed report order through the same function (they must not disagree about which failure matters most), the report still explains why it is not in RPN order, and LIVE that rpn is still generated and S/O/D still bounded 1..10 - deliberately NOT 'sort by our own rule then assert our own rule', which can never fail. Teeth proven twice: reverting the report to rpn order -> FAIL, dropping the severity CHECK -> FAIL. Self-test pins the exact real pair above.
